As for His words "and a prophet from among the righteous", He means: a messenger from his Lord to his people, informing them on His behalf of His command and His prohibition, His lawful and His unlawful, and conveying to them from Him that with which He sent him to them.
By His words "from among the righteous" He means: from among His righteous prophets.

We have already shown in what has gone before the meaning of "prophethood" and what its root is, with the evidences for that and the proofs indicating the correct position concerning it, in a manner that dispenses with repeating it.
### On the interpretation of His words: He said: My Lord, how shall I have a boy, when old age has reached me and my wife is barren? (3:40)

Abū Jaʿfar{{fn:Abū Jaʿfar is al-Ṭabarī's own name of address (kunya); the phrase "Abū Jaʿfar said" marks the commentator's own voice.}} said: He means that Zachariah said, when the angels called out to him "that God gives you glad tidings of John, confirming a Word from God, and a master, and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous": "How shall I have a boy, when old age has reached me?", meaning: one who has reached the age that I have reached has no child born to him; "and my wife is barren".

"The barren" (ʿāqir) among women is she who does not bear children. From it one says "a barren woman" (imraʾah ʿāqir) and "a barren man" (rajul ʿāqir), as ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl{{fn:ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl (d. c. 10/631), chief of the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah and a celebrated warrior-poet; he lost an eye at the battle of Fayf al-Rīḥ and was childless.}} said:
> Wretched indeed would the young man be! If I am one-eyed, childless and a coward too, then what excuse have I in any assembly?
As for "old age" (al-kibar), it is the verbal noun of kabira fa-huwa yakbaru kibaran ("he grew old, so he grows old, with old age").

It has been said: "old age has reached me", whereas He said in another place I have reached, from old age (19:8), because whatever has reached you, you have reached it. Its meaning is only: I have grown old; and it is like the saying of the speaker qad balaghanī al-jahd ("exhaustion has reached me"), in the sense: I am in exhaustion.

If someone says: How could Zachariah, who was the prophet of God, say "My Lord, how shall I have a boy, when old age has reached me and my wife is barren?", when the angels had given him the glad tidings they gave him by the command of God to them? Did he doubt their truthfulness? That is something by which the people of faith in God may not be described, so how then the prophets and the messengers? Or was that from him a denial of the power of his Lord? That is a still greater calamity!
It is said: That was from him (peace be upon him) otherwise than you have supposed; rather, his saying what he said of that was as:

(7001) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: When he heard the call, meaning Zachariah, when he heard the angels' call with the glad tidings of John, Satan came to him and said to him: "O Zachariah, the voice you heard is not from God; it is only from Satan, mocking you! Had it been from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals to you in other matters!" So he doubted on the spot, and said "How shall I have a boy", a male? He says: from where? "when old age has reached me and my wife is barren".

(7002) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Abū Bakr, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Then Satan came to him, wishing to spoil for him the favour of his Lord, and said: "Do you know who called you?" He said: "Yes! The angels of my Lord called me!" He said: "No, rather that was Satan! Had this been from your Lord, He would have kept it hidden to you as you kept your call hidden!" So he said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."

So his saying what he said of that, and his returning to his Lord with the question with which he returned by his words "How shall I have a boy?", was because of the whispering from Satan that had mingled with his heart, so that it made him imagine that the call he had heard was a call from other than the angels; so he said "My Lord, how shall I have a boy?", seeking certainty in his affair, so that it might be established for him, by a sign God would show him in that, that it was glad tidings from God upon the tongues of His angels. For this reason he said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."

It is also possible that his saying this was a question from him to his Lord: from what quarter would the child of whom he had been given glad tidings come? From his wife? She is barren. Or from some other woman? In that case it would be otherwise than the manner stated by ʿIkrimah and al-Suddī and those who said the like of what they said.
### On the interpretation of His words: He said: Thus does God do what He wills (3:40)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He means, Majestic is His praise, by His words "Thus does God": that is, He is as He has described Himself, that it is easy for Him to create a child from an old man who has despaired of offspring and from a barren woman from whose like childbearing is not hoped for, just as He created you, O Zachariah, before the creation of the child from you, when you were nothing; because He is God, for whom the creation of anything He wishes is not difficult, and for whom the doing of anything He wills is not impossible, because His power is the power which no power resembles; as:
(7003) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: "Thus does God do what He wills", and I created you before, when you were nothing.
### On the interpretation of His words: He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign (3:41)

Abū Jaʿfar{{fn:Abū Jaʿfar is al-Ṭabarī himself, speaking in his own voice.}} said: By this He means, Majestic is His praise, reporting about Zachariah: Zachariah said: My Lord, if this call by which I have been called, and the voice which I have heard, is the voice of Your angels and glad tidings from You to me, then appoint for me a sign – that is, a mark – that it is so, so that there may depart from me what Satan has whispered to me and cast into my heart, namely that it is the voice of something other than the angels, and glad tidings from someone other than You. As:

(7004) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said concerning My Lord, appoint for me a sign (3:41): He said – meaning Zachariah –: O Lord, if this voice is from You, then appoint for me a sign.
We have already shown in what has gone before the meaning of "sign" (āya), and that it is a mark (ʿalāma), in a manner that dispenses with repeating it here.
The scholars of Arabic have differed over the reason the Arabs leave this word without a hamza, when their custom is to give a hamza to every yāʾ that comes after a quiescent alif.

- Some of them said: They left it without a hamza because it was originally ayya, and the doubling was heavy for them, so they replaced it with an alif because of the open vowel before the doubled letter, just as they said aymā fulān fa-akhzāhu Allāh ("as for so-and-so, may God disgrace him").{{fn:That is, aymā for ammā with the doubled mīm: the doubling is resolved into a long vowel, as the first group claims happened in āya.}}

- Others among them said: Rather, it is of the pattern fāʿila with a letter dropped (manqūṣa). They were questioned, and it was said to them: Then why is it that the Arabs form its diminutive as uyayya, and do not say uwayya? They said: That is said just as is said of "Fāṭima", "this is Fuṭayma". It was said to them: But they only form the diminutive of fāʿila on the pattern fuʿayla when it is a proper name in the sense of so-and-so, masculine or feminine; as for anything else, it is not their practice to form the diminutive of fāʿila on fuʿayla.{{fn:The holders of this view are al-Kisāʾī and his followers; those who questioned them are al-Farrāʾ and his followers.}}

- Others said: It is of the pattern faʿla, whose first yāʾ was turned into an alif, as was done with ḥāja ("need") and qāma ("stature"). It was said to them: The Arabs only do that with triliteral words. And those who rejected this statement of theirs said: Had it been as they say, one would have said for nawāt ("date-stone") nāya, and for ḥayāt ("life") ḥāya.
### On the interpretation of His words: He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture (3:41)

Abū Jaʿfar said: So God punished him – according to what has been related to us – for his asking for the sign after the angels had addressed him face to face with the glad tidings, and He made his sign, as confirmation that what he had heard from the angels of the glad tidings of John was from God, a sign in his own person. God, Exalted be His mention, thereby combined the mark which he had asked of his Lord, in a manner that made plain to him the truth of the glad tidings, that they were from God, with a purging of him from his slip and from the error of his speech and his request.
The like of what we have said about this was said by a number of the scholars of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl).
### Those who said this

(7005) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words My Lord, appoint for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture (3:41): He was punished with that only because the angels had addressed him face to face with it and given him the glad tidings of John, and he asked for the sign after the angels had spoken to him. So he was seized in his tongue, and he became unable to speak except by what he could signal and indicate; and God, Exalted be His mention, said, as you hear: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture.

(7006) al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words that God gives you glad tidings of John, confirming (3:39): He said: The angels addressed him face to face, and he said My Lord, appoint for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture – He means, except by signalling; and it was a punishment with which he was punished, since he asked for the sign even though the angels had addressed him face to face with that of which they gave him glad tidings.

(7007) al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, concerning His words My Lord, appoint for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture: He said: It was related to us – and God knows best – that he was punished because the angels had addressed him face to face and given him the glad tidings of John, and he asked for the sign afterwards, so he was seized in his tongue.

(7008) I was told on the authority of ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, who said: It was related to us – and God knows best – that he was punished because the angels had addressed him face to face and given him the glad tidings of John, saying that God gives you glad tidings of John (3:39); then, after the angels had spoken to him, he asked for the sign, so his tongue was seized and he became unable to speak except by gesture – meaning, he would signal by signs.

(7009) Abū ʿUbayd al-Waṣṣābī related to me: Muḥammad ibn Ḥimyar related to us: Ṣafwān ibn ʿAmr related to us, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, concerning His words He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture: He said: His tongue swelled in his mouth until it filled it; then God released it after three days.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The reciters chose the subjunctive (naṣb) in His words that you shall not speak to people (allā tukallima) only because the meaning of the sentence is: He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people, in the time to come, for three days. Thus the an is the one that accompanies the future tense, not the one that accompanies nouns and puts them in the accusative. Had the meaning been: Your sign is that you are indeed not speaking to people for three days – that is, that you are in this state for three days – the proper form of the expression would have been the indicative (rafʿ), because an would then have had the sense of the heavy anna lightened. But that was not permissible, because of what I have described, namely that the sense is the other one.

As for "gesture" (ramz), the predominant meaning of it among the Arabs is signalling with the lips, though it is sometimes used of signalling with the eyebrows and the eyes, and that is not common among them. "Ramz" may also be said of hidden speech that is like whispering in a lowered voice; from this is the saying of Juʾayya ibn ʿĀʾidh:{{fn:Juʾayya ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Naṣrī, a pre-Islamic poet of the Hawāzin.}}
> The speech of the champions was a murmur, and a rumbling of theirs like the roar of camels.

From it one says: "So-and-so murmured (ramaza), and he murmurs, yarmizu and yarmuzu, ramzan; and he keeps murmuring, yatarammazu tarammuzan." And one says: "He struck him a blow and he writhed (irtamaza) from it", that is, he convulsed in death. The poet said:
> I fell from her onto the back of my neck, writhing.

The scholars of interpretation have differed over the meaning that God, Mighty and Majestic, intended in His report about Zachariah in His words Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and which of the meanings of "ramz" was intended by it.
- Some of them said: What is meant by it is: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by a movement of the lips, without your tongue articulating the speech.
### Those who said this
(7010) Abū Kurayb related to us: Jābir ibn Nūḥ related to us, from al-Naḍr ibn ʿArabī, from Mujāhid, concerning His words except by gesture: He said: Moving the lips.
(7011) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning three days except by gesture: He said: His signalling with his lips.
(7012) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfa related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
- Others said: Rather, God meant by it signalling and indicating.
### Those who said this
(7013) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: my father related to us, from Salama ibn Nubayṭ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning except by gesture: He said: Indication.

(7014) I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words except by gesture: He said: "Ramz" is that he indicates with his hand or his head and does not speak.

(7015) Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning except by gesture: He said: "Ramz" is that he was seized in his tongue, and he began to speak to people with his hand.
(7016) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, concerning except by gesture: He said: And "ramz" is indication.

(7017) Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words My Lord, appoint for me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture, the verse: He said: He made his sign that he should not speak to people for three days except by gesture, save that he could remember God. And "ramz" is indication: he would indicate to them.
(7018) al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning except by gesture: except by signalling.
(7019) We were told on the authority of ʿAmmār: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, the like of it.
(7020) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning except by gesture: He means: indication.
(7021) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr said concerning except by gesture: except by indication.

(7022) Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAbbād, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture: He said: He was held back in his tongue, and he began to signal with his hand to his people: Glorify God morning and evening.
### On the interpretation of His words: And remember your Lord much, and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning (3:41)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He means by this: God, Majestic is His praise, said to Zachariah: O Zachariah, your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture, without any dumbness, infirmity or illness; and remember your Lord much, for you will not be prevented from remembering Him, nor will anything come between you and glorifying Him and the other forms of remembering Him. And indeed:

(7023) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Abū Maʿshar, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, who said: Had God granted anyone a dispensation to abandon remembrance, He would have granted it to Zachariah, when He said Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture; and remember your Lord much – even so.
As for His words and glorify Him in the evening, He means: magnify your Lord by worshipping Him in the evening.

The "evening" (ʿashiyy) is from the time the sun declines until it sets, as the poet said:{{fn:The poet is Ḥumayd ibn Thawr al-Hilālī, describing a shade-tree (sarḥa) whose shade is jealously guarded.}}
> Neither its shade, in the coolness of the forenoon, can you attain, nor its afternoon shadow, in the coolness of the evening, do you taste.
For the afternoon shadow (fayʾ) begins its return only when the sun declines, and it comes to an end with its setting.

As for "the early morning" (ibkār), it is a verbal noun from one's saying "so-and-so went out early (abkara) on an errand, and he goes out early, yubkiru ibkāran", and that is when he goes out on it between the rising of dawn and the time of forenoon; that is "ibkār". One says of it "abkara fulān" and "bakara yabkuru bukūran". From "ibkār" is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:

> Is it from the people of Nuʿm that you are setting out at morning, departing early?{{fn:Nuʿm was a woman of the Quraysh clan of Jumaḥ whom ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa often celebrated in his verse; this is the opening hemistich of his best-known ode.}}
And from "bukūr" is the saying of Jarīr:

> Lo, Salmā has set out early, and her early setting-out is in earnest, and after unity her commander has split the staff.{{fn:"Splitting the staff" is a proverbial expression for breaking away from the group; "her commander" is the one whose counsel she follows, her husband or her father.}}
And from this one says: "The palms bore early (bakara al-nakhl), yabkuru bukūran, and abkara yubkiru ibkāran"; and the "bākūr" of fruits is the first of them to ripen.
The like of what we have said about this was said by the scholars of interpretation.
### Those who said this

(7024) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning: He said: The early morning is the first part of dawn, and the evening is the declining of the sun until it sets.
(7025) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfa related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
### On the interpretation of His words: And when the angels said: O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds (3:42)

Abū Jaʿfar{{fn:Abū Jaʿfar is al-Ṭabarī himself, speaking in his own voice.}} said: By this He means, Majestic is His praise: And God is Hearing, Knowing, when the wife of ʿImrān said: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, consecrated (3:34–35), and when the angels said: O Mary, God has chosen you.
The meaning of His words has chosen you is: He has selected you and elected you for His obedience and for the honour with which He has singled you out.
His words and purified you mean: He has purified your religion from the doubt and the defilements that are in the religions of the women of the children of Adam.

And chosen you above the women of the worlds: He means: He has selected you above the women of the worlds in your own time, by your obedience to Him, and so He has preferred you over them. As it is related from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "The best of its women is Mary the daughter of ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid" – meaning by his words "the best of its women", the best of the women of the people of Paradise.

(7026) al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī related that to me: Muḥāḍir ibn al-Muwarriʿ related to us: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa related to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, who said: I heard ʿAlī in Iraq say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: The best of its women is Mary the daughter of ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadīja.

(7027) Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: al-Mundhir ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥizāmī related to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The best of the women of Paradise is Mary the daughter of ʿImrān, and the best of the women of Paradise is Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid.

(7028) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words And when the angels said: O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds: It was related to us that the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "Sufficient for you, among the women of the worlds, are Mary the daughter of ʿImrān, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fāṭima the daughter of Muḥammad." Qatādah said: It was related to us that the Prophet of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "The best women who have ridden camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them towards a child in its infancy, and the most careful of them for a husband in what he possesses." Qatādah said: And it was related to us that he used to say: "Had I known that Mary rode camels, I would not have preferred anyone over her."

(7029) al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds: He said: Abū Hurayra used to relate that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The best women who have ridden camels are the righteous women of Quraysh: the most tender of them towards a child, and the most careful of them for a husband in what he possesses." Abū Hurayra said: And Mary never rode a camel.

(7030) I was told on the authority of ʿAmmār: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, concerning His words And when the angels said: O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds: He said: Thābit al-Bunānī used to relate, from Anas ibn Mālik: that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The best women of the worlds are four: Mary the daughter of ʿImrān, Āsiya the daughter of Muzāḥim the wife of Pharaoh, Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fāṭima the daughter of Muḥammad.

(7031) al-Muthannā related to me: Ādam al-ʿAsqalānī related to us: Shuʿba related to us: ʿAmr ibn Murra related to us, saying: I heard Murra al-Hamdānī relate, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Many among men have attained perfection, but none among women attained perfection except Mary, Āsiya the wife of Pharaoh, Khadīja the daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fāṭima the daughter of Muḥammad.

(7032) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū al-Aswad al-Miṣrī related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from ʿUmāra ibn Ghaziyya, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān: that Fāṭima the daughter of Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī related to him: that Fāṭima the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came in one day while I was with ʿĀʾisha, and he spoke to me privately, and I wept; then he spoke to me privately again, and I laughed. ʿĀʾisha asked me about that, and I said: You are in a hurry indeed! Am I to tell you the secret of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him)? So she left me alone. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) died, ʿĀʾisha asked her, and she said: Yes. He spoke to me privately and said: Gabriel used to review the Qurʾān with me once every year, and this year he has reviewed the Qurʾān with me twice; and there is no prophet but that he is given to live half the lifespan of the one who was before him, and my brother Jesus lived one hundred and twenty years, and this is my sixtieth, and I think that I shall die in this year of mine; and no woman among the women of the worlds has been afflicted with the like of what you will be afflicted with, so do not be less than any woman in patience! She said: So I wept. Then he said: You are the mistress of the women of the people of Paradise, except for Mary the Virgin (al-batūl). And he died that year.

(7033) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū al-Aswad related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, that Abū Ziyād al-Ḥimyarī related to him that he heard ʿAmmār ibn Saʿd say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Khadīja has been preferred above the women of my community as Mary was preferred above the women of the worlds.
The like of what we have said about the meaning of His words and purified you – namely, that He has purified your religion from defilement and doubt – was said by Mujāhid.

(7034) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the words of God God has chosen you and purified you: He said: He has made you good in faith.
(7035) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfa related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

(7036) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning and chosen you above the women of the worlds: He said: That is in respect of the worlds of that day.
The angels – according to what Ibn Isḥāq related – used to say this to Mary face to face.

(7037) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salama related to us: Ibn Isḥāq related to me, saying: Mary was confined in the sanctuary (kanīsa), and with her in the sanctuary was a boy named Joseph, whose mother and father had made him a consecrated one, confined there; so they were in the sanctuary together. Whenever Mary's water and Joseph's water ran out, the two of them would take their two water-jars and set off for the open country where there was the water from which they drew their sweet water, and they would fill their two jars and then return to the sanctuary. The angels meanwhile would turn to Mary with: O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of the worlds; and when Zachariah heard that, he would say: Truly the daughter of ʿImrān has some great matter in store!
### On the interpretation of His words: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate, and bow with those who bow (3:43)

Abū Jaʿfar{{fn:Abū Jaʿfar is al-Ṭabarī himself, speaking in his own voice.}} said: By His words, Majestic is His praise – reporting what His angels said to Mary – O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, He means: devote your obedience sincerely to your Lord alone.

We have already shown the meaning of "devout obedience" (qunūt), with its evidences, in what has gone before. The disagreement among the scholars of interpretation about it in this place is like their disagreement about it there. We shall mention the statements of some of them in this place also.
- Some of them said: The meaning of be devoutly obedient is: prolong your standing still.
### Those who said this

(7039) al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfa related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

(7040) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning be devoutly obedient to your Lord: He said: Mujāhid said: Prolong your standing still in prayer – meaning qunūt.

(7042) al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs related to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, who said: When it was said to her O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, she stood until her feet swelled.

He says: Stand for your Lord in prayer. He says: Stand still for your Lord, that is, stand upright for Him in prayer; and prostrate, and bow with those who bow.

### Those who said this

- Others said: Its meaning is: obey your Lord.
### Those who said this
(7048) al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words be devoutly obedient to your Lord: He said: Obey your Lord.
(7049) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning be devoutly obedient to your Lord: Obey your Lord.

(7050) al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb related to us: Ibn Lahīʿa related to us, from Darrāj, from Abū al-Haytham, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: Every passage of the Qurʾān in which qunūt is mentioned, it means obedience to God.

(7051) Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord: He said: He says: Worship your Lord.

Abū Jaʿfar said: We have also explained the meaning of "bowing" (rukūʿ) and "prostration" (sujūd), with the proofs that indicate its soundness, and that both mean humility before God and submission to Him through obedience and servitude.

The interpretation of the verse, then, is: O Mary, devote the worship of your Lord sincerely to His face alone, and humble yourself in obedience to Him and worship of Him together with those of His creatures who humble themselves before Him, in gratitude to Him for the honour He has bestowed upon you of being chosen, of being purified from defilements, and of being preferred above the women of the world of your age.
### On the interpretation of His words: That is of the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you (3:44)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, Majestic is His praise, "That", He means the reports with which He informed His servants concerning the wife of ʿImrān and her daughter Mary, and Zachariah and his son John, and all the rest of what He related in the verses from His words Indeed God chose Adam and Noah (3:33). Then He, Exalted be His mention, gathered all of that together with His word "That", and said: these tidings are "of the tidings of the unseen", that is, of the reports of the unseen.

By "the unseen" He means that they are among the hidden reports of those people, of which neither you, O Muḥammad, nor your people had any knowledge, and which none knew save a few of the learned men (aḥbār) of the people of the two Scriptures and their monks.

Then He, Exalted be His mention, informed His Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) that He revealed that to him, as a proof of his prophethood, a confirmation of his truthfulness, and a cutting-off by it of the excuse of those who denied his message among the unbelievers of the people of the two Scriptures, who know that Muḥammad could not have attained knowledge of these tidings, hidden as they were, nor arrived at acquaintance with them, obscure as they were even among their own people, except by God's making them known to him; since it was known to them that Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was unlettered: he did not write, so as to read books and thereby arrive at knowledge of that from books, nor did he keep company with the people of the Scriptures so as to take his knowledge from them.
As for "the unseen" (al-ghayb), it is a verbal noun from the expression "So-and-so was absent (ghāba) from such a thing; he is absent from it, ghayban and ghaybatan".
As for His words "which We reveal to you", their interpretation is: which We send down to you.

The root sense of "revealing" (al-īḥāʾ) is the casting of something by the one who reveals to the one to whom it is revealed. That may take place by writing, by a sign, by a gesture, by inspiration, and by a message, as He said, Majestic is His praise: And your Lord revealed to the bee (16:68), meaning: He cast that to it and so inspired it; and as He said: And when I revealed to the disciples (5:111), meaning: I cast knowledge of that to them by inspiration; and as the rajaz poet said:{{fn:al-ʿAjjāj.}}
> He revealed to it its fixity, and it stood fixed.

meaning: He cast that to it as a command; and as He said, Majestic is His praise: So he revealed to them that they should glorify morning and evening (19:11), meaning: he cast that to them by gesture. The root sense in it is what I have described, the casting of that to them. His casting of it to them may be by gesture, and it may be by writing. Of this is His word: And indeed the devils reveal to their friends (6:121): they cast that to them by whispering; and His word: And this Qurʾān has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it and whomever it reaches (6:19): it was cast to me through Gabriel's (peace be upon him) coming with it to me from God, Mighty and Majestic.

As for "revelation" (al-waḥy), it is that which falls from the one who reveals to the one to whom it is revealed, and for this reason the Arabs called script and writing waḥy, because it falls upon what is written and remains fixed in it, as Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
> Odes from him have reached the foreigners and the horizons, / enduring as the waḥy endures in the deaf rock.
By which he means: the writing fixed in the rock. It may be said of writing in particular, when the writer writes it, waḥā without the alif; of this is the saying of Ruʾbah:
> As though it were, after the winds that overwhelm it / and the persistent, long-settled rains that batter it, / the gospel of learned men, which its illuminator inscribed (waḥā).
### On the interpretation of His words: and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary (3:44)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, Majestic is His praise, "and you were not with them", He means: you were not, O Muḥammad, in their presence so as to know what We teach you of their reports which you did not witness; rather, you know that and attain acquaintance with it only through Our making it known to you.
The meaning of His words "with them" (ladayhim) is: in their presence (ʿindahum).
The meaning of His words "when they cast" is: at the time they cast their pens.

As for "their pens", they are their arrows with which those of the Children of Israel who drew lots drew their lots over the guardianship of Mary, as we have explained previously regarding His words "and Zachariah took charge of her" (3:37).
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

(7052) Al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Hishām ibn ʿAmr related to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, concerning His words "and you were not with them": He means Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

(7053) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "they cast their pens": Zachariah and his companions drew lots with their pens over Mary when she was brought in to them.
(7054) Al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

(7055) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words "and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary, and you were not with them when they disputed": Mary was the daughter of their leader (imām) and their chief, so the Children of Israel contended with one another over her and cast lots over her with their arrows as to which of them should take charge of her, and Zachariah won the lot over them; he was the husband of her sister,{{fn:That is, the husband of the sister of Mary's mother, as the fuller versions of this report make clear.}} "and Zachariah took charge of her" (3:37): He says, he took her into his care.

(7056) Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words "they cast their pens": he said, they drew lots over Mary as to which of them should take charge of her, and Zachariah won the lot over them.

(7057) Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words "and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary": When Mary was placed in the sanctuary (masjid), the people of the place of prayer cast lots over her, and they were the ones who wrote down the revelation (waḥy); so they cast lots with their pens as to which of them should take charge of her. And God, Mighty and Majestic, said to Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): "and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary, and you were not with them when they disputed".

(7058) I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His words "when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary": they cast lots with their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary, and Zachariah won the lot over them.

(7059) Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to us: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAbbād, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words "and you were not with them when they cast their pens": he said, when they cast lots over Mary; and that was unseen by Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) until God informed him of it.

It was said "which of them should take charge of Mary" only because the casting of their pens by those who drew lots over Mary was so that they might see which of them was most entitled to her guardianship and had the best right to it. So in His words, Mighty and Majestic, "when they cast their pens", there is an indication of something elided from the speech, namely: "so that they might see which of them should take charge of her, and that they might ascertain that and know it".

If anyone supposes that the required case for "which of them" (ayyuhum) is the accusative, since that is its meaning, he supposes wrongly. That is because "seeing", "ascertaining" and "knowing" together with ayy ("which") require a question and an inquiry, and the due of ayy in an inquiry is to stand at the head of its clause, and for the governance of the verb of asking and inquiring upon it to be nullified. For the meaning of the speaker's saying "I shall surely see which of them stood" is "I shall surely inquire of people: which of them stood?", and likewise their saying "I shall surely know".
We have shown previously that the meaning of "take charge of" (yakful) is "take into one's care", in a manner that dispenses with repeating it in this place.
### On the interpretation of His words: and you were not with them when they disputed (3:44)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By that He means, Majestic is His praise: you were not, O Muḥammad, in the presence of Mary's people when they disputed over her as to which of them had the best right to her and was most entitled to her.

This, coming from God, Mighty and Majestic, although it is an address to His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), is a rebuke from Him, Mighty and Majestic, to those of the people of the two Scriptures who denied him. He says: how can the people of unbelief among them doubt you, when you tell them these tidings though you did not witness them, and were not with them on the day they did these things, and are not one who read the books and so learned their story, nor one who sat with the people of those books and so heard their report?
As in:

(7060) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: "and you were not with them when they disputed", that is: you were not with them when they disputed over her. He informs him of the hidden part of the knowledge which they possessed and concealed, in confirmation of his prophethood and as a proof against them by what he brought them of what they had concealed.
### On the interpretation of His words: When the angels said: O Mary, God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (3:45)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, Majestic is His praise, "When the angels said", He means: you were not with them when they disputed, nor were you with them when the angels said: O Mary, God gives you glad tidings.
"Giving glad tidings" (al-tabshīr) is informing a person of news that gladdens him.

His words "of a Word from Him" mean: of a message from God and a report from Him. It is from the saying of the speaker, "So-and-so cast to me a word with which he gladdened me", meaning: he told me news at which I rejoiced; as He said, Majestic is His praise: and His Word which He cast to Mary (4:171), meaning God's glad tidings to Mary of Jesus, which He cast to her.

So the interpretation of the speech is: you were not, O Muḥammad, in the presence of those people when the angels said to Mary: O Mary, God gives you glad tidings of good news from Him, namely a son of yours whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary.
Some people have said (and it is the view of Qatādah) that the "Word" of which God, Mighty and Majestic, said "of a Word from Him", is His saying "Be".
(7061) Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related that to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words "of a Word from Him": he said, His saying "Be".

God, Mighty and Majestic, named him "His Word" because he came about by His Word, just as it is said of a thing that God has decreed, "this is God's decree and His ordinance", meaning: this came about by God's decree and His ordinance; and as He said, Majestic is His praise: and God's command is ever carried out (4:47; 33:37), meaning by it what God commanded, namely the thing commanded which came about by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic.
Others said: rather, it is a name of Jesus by which God named him, just as He named the rest of His creatures with whatever names He willed.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with him) that he said: the "Word" is Jesus.

(7062) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: my father related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words "When the angels said: O Mary, God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him": he said, Jesus is the Word from God.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The view closest to the correct one, in my opinion, is the first: that the angels gave Mary glad tidings of Jesus on behalf of God, Mighty and Majestic, by His message and His Word which He commanded them to cast to her, namely that God would create from her a son without a husband or a male. For this reason He, Mighty and Majestic, said "whose name (ismuhu) is the Messiah", using the masculine, and did not say "her name (ismuhā)" with the feminine, although "Word" (kalimah) is feminine; because what is intended by "Word" is not the sense of a name in the sense of "so-and-so", but rather it carries the meaning of the glad tidings, and so its pronoun was made masculine, just as the pronoun of "offspring" (dhurriyyah), "beast" (dābbah) and of epithets is made masculine, as we have explained before in what has gone by.

So the interpretation of that is as we said just now: that its meaning is "God gives you glad tidings of good news", and then He made clear concerning the good news that it is a son whose name is the Messiah.

One of the grammarians of Baṣrah has claimed that He used the masculine, saying "whose name is the Messiah", though He had said "of a Word from Him" (and "the Word", in his view, is Jesus), only because in meaning it is so; just as He said, Majestic is His praise: lest a soul should say: Alas for me, and then said Nay, My signs came to you, and you denied them (39:56-59); and just as one says Dhū al-Thudayyah ("the one with the little breast"),{{fn:The nickname of the leader of the Khārijites slain at Nahrawān, whose deformed arm ended in a lump of flesh resembling a breast.}} because his hand was short and close to his breasts, so that they treated it as though its name were thadyah; were it not for that, the hāʾ would not have entered into the diminutive.

One of the grammarians of Kūfah said something like the view of the one we have mentioned among the grammarians of Baṣrah, in that the hāʾ refers to "the Word"; but he differed from him as to the reason for which He used the masculine in His word "whose name" when "the Word" precedes it. He claimed that He said "whose name (ismuhu)", though "the Word" had already been put first, and did not say "her name (ismuhā)", because it is the practice of the Arabs to do this with descriptive terms, epithets and names which were not coined to identify the one named by them, as "so-and-so" and "so-and-so" are; such are "offspring" (dhurriyyah), "successor" (khalīfah) and "beast" (dābbah). For this reason it is permissible in his view to say dhurriyyah ṭayyibah ("goodly offspring", with the feminine) and dhurriyyah ṭayyiban (with the masculine), while it is not permissible to say "Ṭalḥah came" or "Mughīrah stood" with feminine verbs.

Some of them rejected the argument of those who argued in this matter from Dhū al-Thudayyah, and said: the hāʾ was introduced into Dhū al-Thudayyah only because what was meant by it was a piece of the breast, just as one says "we were at a piece of meat (laḥmah) and a draught of date-wine (nabīdhah)", meaning a portion of it. This view is close to our own view which we have stated on this matter.

As for His words "whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary", by them He, Majestic is His praise, informed His servants of the lineage of Jesus, and that he is the son of his mother Mary, and thereby denied of him what those of the Christians who deviate concerning God, Majestic is His praise, ascribed to him when they attributed his sonship to God, Mighty and Majestic, and the charge with which the slandering party among the Jews accused his mother; as in:

(7063) Ibn Ḥumayd related it to me: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: "When the angels said: O Mary, God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, eminent in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near", that is: thus was his affair, not what they say about him.

As for "the Messiah" (al-Masīḥ), it is of the pattern faʿīl, transformed from mafʿūl into faʿīl; it is in fact mamsūḥ ("wiped over"), meaning: God wiped over him and so purified him from sins. For this reason Ibrāhīm said: "the Messiah" is the truthful one (al-ṣiddīq) ...{{fn:There is a gap in the manuscripts at this point; what has apparently fallen out is the chain of transmission for this report from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.}}
(7064) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: my father related to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the like of it.
(7065) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the like of it.
Others said: he was wiped over (musiḥa) with blessing.
(7066) Ibn al-Barqī related to us: ʿAmr ibn Abī Salamah related to us, he said: Saʿīd said: He was called "the Messiah" only because he was wiped over with blessing.
### On the interpretation of His words: eminent in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near (3:45)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His word "eminent" (wajīhan) He means: possessed of standing (wajh) and lofty rank with God, and of honour and nobility. From this a man who is noble, and whom kings and people hold in esteem, is called wajīh; one says of it: "So-and-so was not wajīh, but now he has become eminent (wajuha) with eminence (wajāhah)", and "he has indeed standing (wajh) with the ruler, jāh and wajāhah". Jāh is a transposed form: its wāw was shifted from the beginning of the word to the position of its second radical, and so one says jāh, though it is in fact wajh; and the verb formed from jāh is jāha yajūhu. It is heard from the Arabs: "I fear that he will yajūhunī with more than this", meaning: that he will confront me to my face with something greater than it.

As for the accusative of "eminent", it is on account of the "cutting-off" (qaṭʿ){{fn:Qaṭʿ is the Kūfan grammarians' term for what the Baṣrans call the circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).}} from "Jesus", because "Jesus" is definite and "eminent" is indefinite, and it is a description of him. Had it been in the genitive, in agreement with "a Word", that would have been permissible.
With what we have said, namely that its interpretation is "eminent in this world and the Hereafter with God", Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar agreed, according to what has reached us.
(7067) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: "eminent", he said: eminent in this world and the Hereafter with God.

As for His words "and of those brought near", He means that he is among those whom God will bring near on the Day of Resurrection, settling him in His vicinity and drawing him close to Himself; as in:

(7068) Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words "and of those brought near": He says, among those brought near to God on the Day of Resurrection.

(7069) I was told on the authority of ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, regarding His words "and of those brought near": He says, among those brought near to God on the Day of Resurrection.
(7070) Al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, the like of it.
### On the interpretation of His words: and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be of the righteous (3:46)

Abū Jaʿfar said: As for His words "and he will speak to people in the cradle", their meaning is: God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, eminent with God and speaking to people in the cradle.

So "he will speak" (yukallimu), although it is in the indicative, since it has the form of yafʿalu free from any governing particle acting upon it, is in the position of the accusative; it is analogous to the saying of the poet:
> I passed the night feeding them their evening meal with a keen, cutting blade / that strikes true among their shanks, or strikes astray.
As for "the cradle" (al-mahd), by it He means the resting-place of the infant during his suckling; as in:

(7071) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "and he will speak to people in the cradle", he said: the resting-place of the infant during his suckling.

As for His word "and in maturity" (kahlan), it means: and grown to full manhood, beyond boyhood and short of old age; one says of it "a mature man (rajul kahl)" and "a mature woman (imraʾah kahlah)", as the rajaz poet said:{{fn:ʿUdhāfir al-Fuqaymī.}}
> And never after this will I be a hirer-out of camels, / handling the mature woman and the boy.

What He, Majestic is His praise, meant by His words "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity" is: he will speak to people as an infant in the cradle, as a proof of his mother's innocence of that with which the slanderers charged her and as an evidence for him of his prophethood, and as a grown adult after reaching full manhood, by the revelation of God which He reveals to him, and His command and His prohibition, and what He sends down upon him of His Book.

God, Mighty and Majestic, informed His servants of this concerning the affair of the Messiah, and that he was indeed so, even though what generally holds of people is that they speak as mature men and old men, as an argument thereby against those of the people of unbelief in God among the Christians who say falsehood about him: that he was, from the time He brought him into being, a newborn infant and then a mature man, passing through successive states and changing with the passage of times and days over him, from smallness to bigness and from one condition to another; and that, had he been as the deviants say of him, that would not have been possible for him. By this He gave the lie to what the delegation from the people of Najrān said, who disputed with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about him; He argued thereby against them on behalf of His Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and informed them that he was like the rest of the children of Adam, save for the honour by which God singled him out and distinguished him from them; as in:

(7072) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be of the righteous": He informs them of the states through which he would pass in his lifetime, as the children of Adam pass through their lifetimes, small and grown, except that God singled him out with speech in his cradle as a sign of his prophethood and to make known to His servants the workings of His power.

(7073) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be of the righteous": He says, he will speak to them as a small child and as a grown man.

(7074) Al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ: "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity", he said: he will speak to them as a small child and as a grown man.

(7075) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "and in maturity, and he will be of the righteous", he said: the mature man (kahl) is the forbearing one (ḥalīm).

(7076) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: he spoke to them as a small child, as a grown man, and in maturity. And Ibn Jurayj said: Mujāhid said: the mature man is the forbearing one.

(7077) Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAbbād, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity", he said: he spoke to them in the cradle as a babe, and he spoke to them as a grown man.
Others said: the meaning of His word "and in maturity" is that he will speak to them when he appears.
### Those who said this

(7078) Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I heard him, meaning Ibn Zayd, say concerning His words "and he will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity": Jesus has already spoken to them in the cradle, and he will speak to them when he kills the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl), and on that day he will be a mature man.
"In maturity" (kahlan) is in the accusative by coordination with the position of "and he will speak to people".
As for His words "and he will be of the righteous", He means: of their number and of their allies, because the people of righteousness are of one another in religion and merit.

### On the interpretation of His words: She said: My Lord, how shall I have a son when no man has touched me? He said: Thus does God create what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is (3:47)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By that He means, Majestic is His praise: Mary said, when the angels said to her that God gives you glad tidings of a Word from Him, "My Lord, how shall I have a son": from what quarter shall I have a son? Is it through a husband whom I marry and a spouse whom I wed, or will You originate his creation in me without a husband or a male, and without any man touching me? So God said to her: "Thus does God create what He wills", meaning: thus does God create from you a son of yours without any man touching you, and He makes him a sign for people and a lesson; for He creates what He wills and does what He intends, and He gives a child to whom He wills, without a male and through a male, and withholds that from whom He wills among women, even though she have a husband; because the creation of anything He intends to create is not difficult for Him. It is only that He commands, when He intends something whose creation He intends, and says to it: "Be, and it is", whatever He wills, of whatever He wills, and however He wills; as in:

(7079) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: "She said: My Lord, how shall I have a son when no man has touched me? He said: Thus does God create what He wills": He does what He intends and creates what He wills, from a human or from other than a human; "When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be", of whatever He wills and however He wills, "and it is", what He intended.
### On the interpretation of His words: And He will teach him the Book and the Wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel (3:48)
Abū Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the reading of this.

The generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Medina, and some of the reciters of Kūfah, read it wa-yuʿallimuhu ("and He will teach him") with yāʾ, in correspondence with His words "Thus does God create what He wills" followed by "and He will teach him the Book"; so they attached the predicate in His word "and He will teach him" to the like of the predicate in His words "He creates what He wills" and His words "He only says to it: Be, and it is".

The generality of the reciters of Kūfah and some of the Baṣrans read it wa-nuʿallimuhu ("and We will teach him") with nūn, coordinating it with His words "which We reveal to you", as though He said: "That is of the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you" and "We will teach him the Book". They said: what comes after "We reveal" belongs to its clause as far as His words "Be, and it is", and then "and We will teach him" is coordinated with it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view on this in our opinion is that they are two different readings, not different in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads, he attains what is correct in that, because the meaning of the two readings agrees, in that it is a report from God that He will teach Jesus the Book and whatever else He mentioned that He will teach him.

This is the beginning of a report from God, Mighty and Majestic, to Mary of what He would do with the son of whom He gave her glad tidings, by way of honour, elevation of rank and excellence. He said: thus does God create from you a son, without a male or a husband, and He will teach him the Book, which is the script he writes with his hand; and the Wisdom, which is the normative practice (sunnah) which He reveals to him outside of a book; and the Torah, which is the Torah that was sent down to Moses and had been among them since the time of Moses; and the Gospel, the Gospel of Jesus, which did not exist before him, but God informed Mary before the creation of Jesus that He would reveal it to him.

He informed her of that and named it to her only because she had already learned, from what had been sent down in the Scriptures, that God would send a prophet to whom a book named the Gospel would be revealed; so God, Mighty and Majestic, informed her that that prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) whose description she had heard, the one of whom He had promised His prophets before that He would send down upon him the book called the Gospel, was the son whom He had granted her and of whom He had given her glad tidings.
A group of the people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this
(7080) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: "and We will teach him the Book", he said: with his hand.
(7081) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: "and We will teach him the Book and the Wisdom", he said: the Wisdom is the sunnah.

(7082) Al-Muthannā related to us: Isḥāq related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from Qatādah, concerning His words "and We will teach him the Book and the Wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel", he said: "the Wisdom" is the sunnah; "and the Torah and the Gospel", he said: Jesus used to recite the Torah and the Gospel.
(7083) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "and We will teach him the Book and the Wisdom", he said: the Wisdom is the sunnah.

(7084) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, who said: He informed her, meaning God informed Mary, of what He intended for him, and said: "and He will teach him the Book and the Wisdom and the Torah", which had been among them since the time of Moses, "and the Gospel", another book which He newly brought forth to him, of which they had no knowledge save the mention of it by the prophets before him, that it would come to be.
### On the interpretation of His words: and a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" (3:49)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, Majestic is His praise, and a messenger, He means: and We shall make him a messenger to the Children of Israel. The mention of "and We shall make him" was left out because the discourse itself points to it, as the poet said:
> And you saw your husband in the fray,

> girded with a sword and a lance.{{fn: The verse is a stock grammatical example: "girded" governs "sword", while a verb such as "bearing" must be understood for "lance"; so here "We shall make him" is understood before "a messenger".}}

And His words "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord" mean: and We shall make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, announcing that he is My prophet, My bearer of good tidings and My warner. And my proof of my truthfulness in that is: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord", meaning: with a token from your Lord which verifies my word and confirms my report that I am a messenger to you from your Lord. As:

(7085) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: and a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord", that is: by which my prophethood is verified, that I am a messenger from Him to you.
### On the interpretation of His words: "I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by God's leave" (3:49)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By that He means, Majestic is His praise: and a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord"; then He explained what that sign is, and said: "I create for you".

So the interpretation of the passage is: and a messenger to the Children of Israel, announcing that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, in that I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird.
Al-ṭayr ("birds") is the plural of ṭāʾir ("a bird").
The reciters differed over the reading of this.

Some of the people of the Ḥijāz read it "the likeness of a bird (al-ṭāʾir), then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird (ṭāʾiran)", in the singular.{{fn: The singular forms belong to the Medinan reading tradition, associated with Nāfiʿ and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī.}}
Others read it "the likeness of birds (al-ṭayr), then I breathe into it and it becomes birds (ṭayran)", in the plural in both places.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The reading I find most pleasing in this is the reading of those who read "the likeness of birds, then I breathe into it and it becomes birds", in the plural in both places together, because this was among the attributes of Jesus, that he did this by God's leave, and because it conforms to the script of the codex (muṣḥaf). Following the script of the codex, when the meaning is sound and the reading is widely transmitted, is more pleasing to me than departing from the codex.
Jesus's creating of what he used to create of birds took place as:

(7086) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us: Ibn Isḥāq related to us: that Jesus, God's blessings be upon him, sat one day with some boys from the elementary school (kuttāb). He took some clay and then said: "Shall I make for you a bird out of this clay?" They said: "Can you really do that?" He said: "Yes, by my Lord's leave." Then he shaped it, and when he had put it into the form of a bird he breathed into it and then said: "Be a bird, by God's leave," and it went out flying from between his two palms. The boys went out with this news of his doing and told their teacher about it, and he spread it among the people. He grew up, and the Children of Israel plotted against him; and when his mother feared for him she carried him on a little donkey of hers and went out with him in flight.
It is mentioned that when he wished to create the bird out of clay he asked them: "Which bird is hardest in its make-up?" He was told: "The bat." As:

(7087) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said, concerning His words "I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird": he said: "Which bird is hardest in its make-up?" They said: "The bat; it is nothing but flesh." He said: So he did it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: If someone asks: How is it said "then I breathe into it" (fīhi, masculine), when it has already been said "I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird", and "likeness" (hayʾah) is feminine?

It is said: Because the meaning of the passage is: then I breathe into the bird. Had it been "then I breathe into it" (fīhā, feminine), it would have been correct and permissible, as He said in al-Māʾidah, then you breathe into it (5:110), meaning: then you breathe into the form. It has been mentioned that in one of the two readings it is "then I breathe it" (fa-anfukhuhā), without "into".{{fn: Al-Farrāʾ attributes this reading to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.}} The Arabs do the like of this, saying: "Many a night I have spent" (bittuhā), and "I have spent in it" (bittu fīhā). The poet said:{{fn: Yazīd ibn Rabīʿah ibn Mufarrigh al-Ḥimyarī, from his lampoon on ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād after the latter's death at the battle of the Zāb.}}
> No collar was rent, no wailing woman stood over you,
> and no steeds wept for you beside the spoils of the slain.
meaning: "nor stood over you" (qāmat ʿalayka), the preposition being dropped. And as another said:
> One of the daughters of Banū ʿAyyidh Allāh — a man sweet of nature has gone off with her

> until the Trumpet is blown (yunfakhu al-ṣūr).{{fn: The witness is "the Trumpet is blown", where the verb takes its object directly rather than with "into", as in the Qur'anic "it is blown into the Trumpet".}}
### On the interpretation of His words: "and I heal the blind from birth and the leper" (3:49)

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words "and I heal" (ubriʾu) He means: and I cure. One says of it: "God healed (abraʾa) the sick man", when He has cured him of his illness, "and He heals him (yubriʾuhu), a healing (ibrāʾan)"; and "the sick man recovered (baraʾa), and he recovers (yabraʾu), a recovery (barʾan)"; and it is also said "the sick man recovered (bariʾa), and he recovers (yabraʾu)": two well-known dialectal forms.
The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of al-akmah.
- Some of them said: He is the one who cannot see by night but sees by day.
### Those who said this

(7088) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words "and I heal the akmah": he said: The akmah is the one who sees by day and does not see by night, so that he gropes about blindly (yatakammah).
(7089) Al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
- Others said: He is the blind man whose mother bore him so.
### Those who said this
(7090) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: We used to be told that the akmah is the one who is born blind, his eyes covered over.

(7091) Al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from Qatādah, concerning His words "and I heal the blind from birth and the leper": he said: We used to be told that the akmah is the one who is born blind, with his eyes closed shut.
(7092) I was told, from al-Minjāb: Bishr related to us, from ʿUmārah, from Abū Rawq, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The akmah is the one who is born blind.
- Others said: Rather, he is the blind man.
### Those who said this
(7093) Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: "and I heal the akmah": he is the blind man.
(7094) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: The blind man.
(7095) Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words "and I heal the akmah": he said: The akmah is the blind man.
(7096) Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me: Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī related to us, from ʿAbbād ibn Manṣūr, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words "and I heal the akmah": he said: The blind man.
- Others said: He is the weak-sighted (aʿmash).
### Those who said this
(7097) Al-Muthannā related to me: Isḥāq related to us: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar related to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words "and I heal the akmah": he said: The weak-sighted.

Abū Jaʿfar said: What is known among the Arabs as the meaning of kamah is blindness. One says of it: "his eye went blind (kamihat), and it goes blind (takmahu), a blinding (kamahan)", and "I blinded it (akmahtuhā)", when you have made it blind, as Suwayd ibn Abī Kāhil said:
> It blinded his eyes until they turned white,

> so he reproaches himself, now that he has desisted.{{fn: From Suwayd's famous ode in the Mufaḍḍaliyyāt: the poet likens himself to an unassailable rock at which his enemy keeps hurling stones until his eyes fail him.}}
And from it is the saying of Ruʾbah:
> I shouted him down, and he recoiled with the recoiling of a man born blind
> amid the destroying pitfalls of one bewildered and babbling.

God, Mighty and Majestic, reported of Jesus, God's blessings be upon him, that he said this to the Children of Israel only as his argument against them, by these lessons and signs, for his prophethood. That is because blindness from birth and leprosy have no treatment by which one versed in medicine could cure the sufferer by remedy. So this was among his proofs of the truth of his saying that he was a messenger of God, since it is one of the miracles (muʿjizāt), together with the other signs that God gave him as evidence of his prophethood.

As for what ʿIkrimah said, that kamah is weakness of sight, and what Mujāhid said, that it is poor sight by night, there is no sense in either of them. For God does not argue against His creatures with an argument in which they would have a way of opposing Him. Had it been among that with which Jesus argued against the Children of Israel for his prophethood that he cured the weak-sighted, or the one who sees by day and does not see by night, they would have been able to oppose him by saying: "There is no proof for you in this; among us are people who treat that, and they are neither prophets nor messengers of God."

In this there is clear evidence of the soundness of what we have said, that the akmah is the blind man who sees nothing, neither by night nor by day. And it is closer to what Qatādah said, that he is one born so, because the treatment of such a case is not claimed by any human being except one to whom God has given the like of what He gave to Jesus; and likewise the treatment of the leper.
### On the interpretation of His words: "and I give life to the dead by God's leave, and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses" (3:49)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Jesus's giving life to the dead was by supplication to God: he would pray for them, and He would answer him. As:

(7098) Muḥammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar related to me: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil related to me: that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Jesus reached twelve years of age, God revealed to his mother, while she was in the land of Egypt — for she had fled with him from her people to the land of Egypt when she gave birth to him — "Go up with him to Syria (al-Shām)." She did what she was commanded. She remained in Syria until he was thirty years old, and his prophethood lasted three years; then God raised him up to Himself. He said: And Wahb claimed that there would sometimes gather around Jesus, in a single assembly, fifty thousand of the sick; whoever of them was able to reach him reached him, and whoever of them was not able to do so, Jesus came to him, walking to him. And he treated them only by supplication to God.

As for His words "and I inform you of what you eat", He means: and I tell you what you eat, of that which I have not seen with my own eyes nor witnessed with you at the time you ate it; "and what you store up", by that He means: and what you put away and hide and do not eat.

He was teaching them that among his proofs of his prophethood too — alongside the miracles which he had informed them he would bring as proof of his prophethood and of his truthfulness in his report that God had sent him to them, namely the creating of birds from clay, the healing of the blind from birth and the leper, and the giving of life to the dead by God's leave, which no human being is capable of except one to whom God has given it as a token for him of his truthfulness and a sign for him of the reality of his word, from among His prophets and messengers and those of His creatures whom He loves — was his informing them of the unseen, to which no human being whose way is like his way has any access.

Abū Jaʿfar said: If someone asks: What proof of his truthfulness was there for him in his saying to them "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses", when we have seen astrologers and soothsayers tell of such things frequently and hit the mark?

It is said: As for the astrologer and the soothsayer, it is known of the two of them, by those whom they inform of such things, that they announce it by extracting it through certain means that lead to knowledge of it. It was not so with Jesus, God's blessings be upon him, nor with the rest of God's prophets and messengers. Rather, Jesus informed of it without any extraction and without seeking knowledge of it by contrivance, but at the outset, by God's making it known to him, with no prior basis that he copied, or built upon, or resorted to, as the astrologer resorts to his calculation and the soothsayer to his familiar spirit (raʾiyy).{{fn: A raʾiyy is a jinn companion who is said to appear to a soothsayer and feed him his false reports of unseen matters.}} That is the distinction between the prophets' knowledge of unseen things and their reporting of them, and the knowledge of all the others who lie against God or claim knowledge of such things. As:

(7099) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: When Jesus reached nine or ten years or thereabouts, his mother put him into the elementary school — so they claim. He was with one of the schoolmasters, who taught him as boys are taught; and the master would not set about teaching him anything of what boys are taught but Jesus anticipated him in knowing it before he taught it to him, so that he would say: "Do you not marvel at this widow's son? I do not go to teach him anything but I find him more knowledgeable in it than I!"

(7100) Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: When Jesus grew up his mother handed him over to learn the Torah. He used to play with the boys, the boys of the village in which he was, and he would tell the boys what their fathers were doing.

(7101) Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: Hushaym related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His words "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses": he said: Jesus son of Mary, when he was in the elementary school, used to tell them what they ate in their houses and what they stored up.

(7102) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Hushaym related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim informed us, who said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses": he said: Jesus son of Mary used to say to a boy in the school: "So-and-so, your family have hidden away such-and-such food for you; will you give me some of it to eat?"

Abū Jaʿfar said: Thus did the prophets and their proofs: of the proofs they bring, they bring that which can be reached by certain contrivances, but not in the manner in which others bring it; rather, in a manner by which creatures know that it cannot be reached in that way by any contrivance except from God.
Something near to what we have said about the interpretation of His words "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses" was said by the people of interpretation.
### Those who said this

(7103) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning God's words "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses": he said: What you ate last night, and what you hid away of it — it is Jesus son of Mary who says it.
(7104) Al-Muthannā related to me: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

(7105) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ said — meaning concerning His words "and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses" — he said: The food and the things they stored up in their houses: an unseen matter which God made known to him.
