- A group of the Companions and the Successors read it hal tastaṭīʿu with a tāʾ and rabbaka in the accusative{{fn:That is, "are you able [to ask] your Lord?", with Jesus as the subject of the verb and "your Lord" as its object, instead of the standard reading "is your Lord able?".}}, meaning: are you able to ask your Lord? or: are you able to call upon your Lord? or: are you able, and do you see fit, to call upon Him? They said: the disciples were not in doubt that God, Exalted be His mention, was able to send that down to them; they only said to Jesus: are you yourself able to do that?

(12993) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Muḥammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: ʿĀʾishah said: The disciples did not doubt that God was able to send down a table to them, but they said: O Jesus, are you able to ask your Lord (hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka)?

(12994) Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf al-Taghlibī related to me: al-Qāsim ibn Sallām related to us: Ibn Mahdī related to us, from Jābir ibn Yazīd ibn Rifāʿah, from Ḥassān ibn Mukhāriq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that he read it thus, hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka, and said: are you able to ask your Lord. And he said: Do you not see that they were believers?

- The generality of the reciters of Medina and Iraq read it hal yastaṭīʿu with a yāʾ and rabbuka in the nominative, meaning: that your Lord should send down to us; just as a man says to his companion, "Are you able to rise up with us in such-and-such a matter?" while he knows that he is able, but means only: will you rise up with us in it? It is also possible that the intention of one who reads it thus is: will your Lord respond to you and comply with you in sending down to us?

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of those who read it hal yastaṭīʿu with a yāʾ and rabbuka with "the Lord" in the nominative, meaning: will He respond to you, if you ask Him for that, and comply with you in it?

We have said that this is the more correct of the two readings only because of what we explained before, that His words "when the disciples said" are connected to "when I inspired", and that the meaning of the speech is: And when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and in My messenger, when the disciples said: O Jesus son of Mary, is your Lord able? If that is so, then it is clear that God, Exalted be His mention, disapproved of what they said in this and regarded it as grave, and commanded them to repent and to return to faith from that saying of theirs, and to acknowledge God's power over all things, and to believe His messenger in the reports he gave them about their Lord. And Jesus said to them, when they said that to him, regarding what they had said as grave: "Fear God, if you are believers." So in God's calling them to repentance, and His summoning them to faith in Him and in His messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) when they said what they said in this, and in the prophet of God's (peace and blessings be upon him) regarding their words as grave, there is indication sufficient, over and above anything else, of the correctness of the reading of this with the yāʾ and "the Lord" in the nominative; for there would have been no sense, in what they said to Jesus, had they said to him "are you able to ask your Lord to send down to us a table from heaven?", for it to be regarded as grave to this degree.

If someone supposes that their saying that to him was regarded as grave on their part only because it was on their part a request for a sign, then he has supposed wrongly. For a sign is asked of the prophets only by one who disbelieves in it, so that the reality of its establishment and the soundness of its matter may be settled for him; as was the request which Quraysh made of our Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), those of the idolaters of his people who asked him, that he turn al-Ṣafā into gold for them and make rivers gush forth through the valleys of Mecca; and as was the request for the she-camel made of Ṣāliḥ by the deniers among his people; and the request made of Shuʿayb, by the unbelievers among those to whom he was sent, that he make a fragment of the sky fall down.

So if those who asked Jesus to ask his Lord to send down to them a table from heaven made their request in this manner, then those who read it with the tāʾ and "the Lord" in the accusative have placed them in a position graver than the position from which they supposed they were steering them away. Or else they asked that of Jesus while certain that he was a prophet of God sent forth and a messenger dispatched, and that God, Exalted be His mention, was able to do what they asked of that.

If they asked that while being so, and their request to him for it was only in the manner in which one of them might ask his prophet, if he were poor, to ask his Lord on his behalf to enrich him, or, if some need arose for him, to ask his Lord on his behalf to fulfil it, then that is in no way a request for a sign; rather it is the request of one who has a need, which has arisen for him, of his Lord, so he asked his prophet to ask his Lord to fulfil it for him.

But God's report, Exalted be His mention, about the people tells of something other than that. For they said to Jesus, when he said to them "Fear God, if you are believers": "We wish to eat of it, and that our hearts be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth." This saying of theirs has made known that they did not know that Jesus had told them the truth, nor were their hearts at rest concerning the reality of his prophethood. There is no statement clearer than this speech that the people's hearts had been touched by sickness and doubt in their religion and in believing their messenger, and that they asked what they asked of that by way of testing.
Those of the people of interpretation said something like what we have said in this.
### Those who said this

(12995) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he used to relate about Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said to the Children of Israel: Would you fast for God thirty days, then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the wage of the labourer is owed by the one for whom he labours! So they did so, then said: O teacher of goodness, you told us, "the wage of the labourer is owed by the one for whom he labours", and you commanded us to fast thirty days, and we did so; and we never laboured thirty days for anyone without his feeding us food when we finished. So is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven? Jesus said: Fear God, if you are believers. They said: We wish to eat of it, and that our hearts be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among the witnesses to it, up to His words I punish no one of the worlds (5:112–115). He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven on which were seven fish and seven loaves, until they set it down before them, and the last of the people ate of it as the first of them had eaten of it.

(12996) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to me: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: Is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?: they said: Will your Lord comply with you, if you ask Him? So God sent down to them a table from heaven on which was every food except meat, and they ate of it.
As for "the table" (māʾidah), it is the active participle from "māda fulānun al-qawma yamīduhum maydan", when a man feeds a people and provisions them; and from this is the saying of Ruʾbah:
> We bring the heads of the pampered rivals as gifts
> to the Commander of the Faithful, the one of whom gifts are sought (al-mumtād).

By his words "al-mumtād" he means the one of whom a gift is asked. So "the māʾidah" is that which feeds; the dining-tray (khiwān) is called by that name because it feeds the eater from what is upon it. And "al-māʾid" is the one who is made to reel at sea; one says "māda yamīdu maydan".

As for His words "He said: Fear God, if you are believers", He means: Jesus said to the disciples who had said to him "is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?": Be watchful of God, O people, and fear Him, lest a punishment from God descend upon you for this saying of yours; for nothing that God wills is beyond Him, and in your doubting God's power to send down a table from heaven there is disbelief in Him; so fear God, lest He send down His vengeance upon you. "If you are believers", he says: if you believe me in what I threaten you with of God's punishing you for your saying, "is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?"

### On the interpretation of His words: They said: We wish to eat of it, and that our hearts be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among the witnesses to it (5:113)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He means by this, Exalted be His mention: the disciples said, answering Jesus for his words to them, "Fear God, if you are believers", concerning your saying to me "is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?": We said that, and asked you to ask our Lord on our behalf, only so that we might eat of the table and so know with certainty His power over all things; "and that our hearts be at rest", He says: and that our hearts be calmed and settled upon His oneness and His power over all that He wishes and wills; "and that we may know that you have told us the truth": and that we may know that you did not lie to us in your report that you are a messenger dispatched by God and a prophet sent forth; "and that we may be to it", He says: and that we may be, regarding the table, "among the witnesses", He says: among those who testify that God sent it down as a proof for Himself against us of His oneness and His power over what He wishes, and for you, of your truthfulness in your prophethood.

### On the interpretation of His words: Jesus son of Mary said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, to be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You; and provide for us, for You are the best of providers (5:114)

Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a report from God, Exalted be His mention, about His prophet Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), that he granted the people what they asked in the matter of asking his Lord for a table to come down to them from heaven.
Then the people of interpretation differed over the interpretation of His words "to be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us".
- Some of them said: its meaning is: we shall take the day on which it came down as a festival (ʿīd) which we and those after us shall honour.
### Those who said this

(12997) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to me: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His words to be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us: he says: we shall take the day on which it came down as a festival which we and those after us shall honour.

(12998) Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words to be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us: he said: they wanted it to be for their descendants after them.

(12999) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven, to be a festival for us, for the first of us: he said: those of them who were alive on that day; and the last of us: those of them who came after them.
(13000) Al-Ḥārith related to me: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Sufyān said: to be a festival for us: they said: we shall pray on it. It came down twice.
- Others said: its meaning is: we shall all eat of it.
### Those who said this

(13001) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Layth, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said: The last of the people ate of it, meaning of the table, when it was set down before them, as the first of them had eaten of it.
- Others said: the meaning of His words "a festival" (ʿīdan) is: a benefit (ʿāʾidah) coming back from God, Exalted be His mention, upon us, and a proof and a demonstration.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the views is the view of those who said: "Its meaning is: to be a festival for us, on which we worship our Lord on the day on which it comes down and pray to Him on it, as people worship on their festivals"; because what is known of the speech of people in use among them for "festival" is what we have mentioned, not the view of those who said, "its meaning is: a benefit from God upon us". And directing the meanings of God's speech to what is known in the speech of those who were addressed by it is preferable to directing them to what is unknown among them, so long as a way to that is found.

As for His words "for the first of us and the last of us", the more correct of its interpretations is the view of those who said: "Its interpretation is: for those of us alive today, and for those of us who come after us", for the reason we mentioned concerning His words "to be a festival for us", because that is the predominant sense of its meaning.

As for His words "and a sign from You", its meaning is: and a mark and a proof from You, O Lord, for Your servants, of Your oneness and of my truthfulness, in that I am a messenger to them with that with which You have sent me; "and provide for us, for You are the best of providers": and give us of Your giving, for You, O Lord, are the best of those who give and the most generous of those who bestow favour, because no reproach and no stinting enters into His giving.
The people of interpretation differed concerning "the table": whether it was sent down to them or not, and what it was.

- Some of them said: It came down, and it was fish and food, and the people ate of it; but it was raised up, after it had come down, because of things they newly committed between themselves and God, Exalted be His mention.
### Those who said this

(13002) Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who said: The table came down as bread and fish.
(13003) Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣudāʾī related to me: my father related to us, from al-Fuḍayl, from ʿAṭiyyah, who said: "The table" was a fish in which was the taste of every food.
(13004) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Fuḍayl, from Masrūq, from ʿAṭiyyah, who said: "The table" was fish in which was something of the taste of every food.
(13005) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: The table came down as bread and fish.

(13006) Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: There came down to Jesus son of Mary and the disciples a dining-tray on which were bread and fish, from which they would eat wherever they alighted, whenever they wished.

(13007) Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: al-Mundhir ibn al-Nuʿmān informed us that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven, to be a festival for us: he said: There came down to them a loaf of barley and some fish. Al-Ḥasan said: Abū Bakr{{fn:That is, ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn Hammām al-Ṣanʿānī, whose agnomen was Abū Bakr.}} said: I related it to ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil, and he said: I heard Wahb, when it was said to him, "And what good would that have done them?", say: Nothing; but God poured blessing in among their folds, so that a group would eat and then go out, and others would come and eat and then go out, until all of them had eaten and left some over.
(13008) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: ʿUbayd Allāh related to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, who said: It is food that came down to them wherever they alighted.

(13009) Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the words of God, Exalted be His mention, a table from heaven: he said: a table on which was food; they were brought it when the punishment was set before them should they disbelieve. Kinds of food came down to them.

(13010) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Abū Maʿshar, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh: that the table came down to Jesus son of Mary with seven loaves and seven fish upon it, of which they would eat what they wished. He said: Then some of them stole from it and said, "Perhaps it will not come down tomorrow!", and so it was raised up.

(13011) Al-Muthannā related to us: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Dāwūd related to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from a man of the Banū ʿIjl, who said: I prayed beside ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, and when he finished he said: Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was? He said: I said: No! He said: They asked Jesus son of Mary for a table on which there would be food from which they would eat and which would not run out. He said: So it was said to them: It will remain with you so long as you do not hide away, or act treacherously, or put aside; if you do so, I shall punish you with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds! He said: Their day was not out before they had hidden away and put aside and acted treacherously, and they were punished with a punishment with which no one of the worlds had been punished. And you, O company of Arabs, used to follow the tails of camels and sheep; then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose standing and lineage you know, and He informed you by the tongue of your Prophet that you will prevail over the Arabs, and He forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, night and day will not pass away before you hoard them both, and He punishes you with a painful punishment.

(13012) Al-Ḥasan ibn Qazaʿah al-Baṣrī related to us: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from Khilās ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The table came down as bread and meat, and they were commanded not to act treacherously nor to store up nor to put aside for the morrow; but they acted treacherously and stored up and put aside, and so they were transformed into apes and swine.

(13013) Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bazīʿ related to me: Yūsuf ibn Khālid related to us: Nāfiʿ ibn Mālik related to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the table: he said: It was food that came down to them from heaven wherever they alighted.
### Those who said this

(13014) Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Khilās ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAmmār, who said: The table came down with fruit of the fruits of Paradise upon it, and they were commanded not to hide away nor act treacherously nor store up. He said: But the people acted treacherously and hid away and stored up, and so God turned them into apes and swine.

(13015) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that it was a table onto which fruit of the fruits of Paradise came down, and they were commanded not to hide away nor act treacherously nor store up for the morrow, as a trial with which God tried them; and whenever they did any of that, Jesus would inform them of it. But the people acted treacherously in it, and hid away and stored up for the morrow.
- Others said: On it was every food except meat.
### Those who said this

(13016) Abū Kurayb related to us: Jarīr related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Maysarah, who said: When the table was set down for the Children of Israel, hands would pass to and fro upon it with every kind of food.
(13017) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Sharīk, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Maysarah and Zādhān, who both said: Hands would pass to and fro upon it with every kind of food.

(13018) Al-Ḥārith related to me: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz related to us: Sufyān al-Thawrī related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān and Maysarah, concerning is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?: they both said: They saw hands passing to and fro upon it with everything except meat.
- Others said: God did not send down a table to the Children of Israel.
Then those who held this view differed.
- Some of them said: This is only a parable which God, Exalted be His mention, set forth for His creation, by which He forbade them to ask God's prophet for signs.
### Those who said this

(13019) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam related to us, from Sharīk, from Layth, from Mujāhid, concerning His words send down to us a table from heaven: he said: A parable that was set forth; nothing came down to them.

- Others said: When it was said to the people, "whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds", they asked to be excused from it, and so it did not come down.
### Those who said this

(13020) Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: Al-Ḥasan used to say: When it was said to them whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, to the end of the verse, they said: We have no need of it; and so it did not come down.
(13021) Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Zādhān, from al-Ḥasan: that he said concerning the table: It did not come down.

(13022) Al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Qāsim ibn Sallām related to us: Ḥajjāj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: A table on which was food; they refused it when the punishment was set before them should they disbelieve, and so they refused that it should come down to them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct view in our opinion on this is to say: God, Exalted be His mention, sent down the table to those who asked Jesus to make that request of his Lord.

We have said this only because of the report which we have related on this from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and his Companions and the people of interpretation after them, apart from the one who stood alone with what we have mentioned from him.

Moreover, God, Exalted be His mention, does not break His promise, nor does any breach occur in His report; and He, Exalted be His mention, said, reporting in His Book about His answer to His prophet Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) when he asked Him what he asked of that: "I am sending it down to you". It is not permissible that He, Exalted be His mention, should say "I am sending it down to you" and then not send it down, because that from Him, Exalted be His mention, is a report, and from Him there comes no contravening of what He reports. Were it permissible for Him to say "I am sending it down to you" and then not send it down to them, it would be permissible for Him to say "whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds", and then for one of them to disbelieve after that and He not punish him; and then neither His promise nor His threat would have any reality or soundness. And it is not permissible that our Lord, Exalted be His mention, be described in that way.

As for the correct view regarding what was on the table, it is to say: on it was something to be eaten. It is possible that it was fish and bread, and it is possible that it was fruit of the fruits of Paradise; knowledge of it brings no benefit and ignorance of it brings no harm, so long as the one who recites the verse affirms the apparent sense of what the revelation admits.

### On the interpretation of His words: God said: I am sending it down to you; but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds (5:115)

Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an answer from God, Exalted be His mention, to the people concerning what they asked their prophet Jesus to ask their Lord, namely His sending down a table to them. He said, Exalted be His mention: I am sending it down to you, O disciples, and feeding you from it; "but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards", He says: whoever of you denies, after My sending it down to you and My feeding you from it, My message to him, and rejects the prophethood of My prophet Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), and opposes obedience to Me in what I have commanded him and forbidden him, "I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds", that is, of the worlds of his own time. And the people did so: they denied and disbelieved after it had been sent down to them, as has been mentioned to us, and they were punished, as has reached us, by being transformed into apes and swine; as in the following:

(13023) Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words I am sending it down to you, the verse: It was mentioned to us that they were turned into swine.

(13024) Ibn Bashshār related to us: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from ʿAwf, from Abū al-Mughīrah al-Qawwās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: The most severely punished of people are three: the hypocrites, those of the people of the table who disbelieved, and the house of Pharaoh.

(13025) Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafah related to us: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān related to us, from ʿAwf, who said: I heard Abū al-Mughīrah al-Qawwās say: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: The most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection are: those of the people of the table who disbelieved, the hypocrites, and the house of Pharaoh.

(13026) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His words but whoever of you disbelieves afterwards: after the table had come to him; I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds: He says: I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds other than the people of the table.

### On the interpretation of His words: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it (5:116)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He, Exalted be His mention, says: On the day when God will gather the messengers and say: What answer were you given? (5:109), "when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"
It was said: God said these words to Jesus when He raised him up to Himself in this world.
### Those who said this

(13028) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?: he said: When God raised Jesus son of Mary up to Himself, the Christians said what they said, and claimed that Jesus had commanded them to do so; so He asked him about his words, and he said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your self. Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen things, up to His words and You are witness over all things (5:116–117).
- Others said: Rather, this is a report from God, Exalted be His mention, that He will say this to Jesus on the Day of Resurrection.
### Those who said this

(13029) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?: he said: while the people were listening; and he answered Him with what you have seen, and acknowledged servanthood for himself before Him, so that whoever used to say about Jesus what he used to say knew that he had only been speaking falsehood.

(13030) Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Jarīr related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Maysarah, who said: God said: O Jesus, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? And his joints trembled, and he feared that he might have said it, and he said: Glory be to You! If I had said it, You would have known it, the verse.

(13031) Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?: When will that be? He said: On the Day of Resurrection; do you not see that He says, This is the day when the truthful will profit from their truthfulness (5:119)?

On this interpretation which Ibn Jurayj gave, "and when" (wa-idh) must have the meaning of "and when" in the sense of the future (wa-idhā), as He said in another place: And if you could see when they are terrified (34:51), meaning: when they will be terrified; and as Abū al-Najm said:
> Then may God reward him on our behalf, when (idh) He rewards,
> with Gardens of Eden in the lofty upper chambers.
meaning: when He will reward (idhā jazā); and as al-Aswad{{fn:Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur al-Nahshalī, the pre-Islamic poet known as the Aʿshā of the Banū Nahshal.}} said:
> So now, when (idh) I jest with them, they only
> say: Lo, the old man has not gone the right way!
meaning: when I jest with them (idhā hāzaltuhunna).

It is as though those who held Ibn Jurayj's view on this directed the interpretation of the verse to: "whoever of you disbelieves afterwards, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one of the worlds" in this world, and I shall punish him also in the Hereafter, "when God says: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two views in our opinion on this is the view of those who held the view of al-Suddī, namely that God, Exalted be His mention, said that to Jesus when He raised him up to Himself, and that the report is a report about what has passed, for two reasons:

- One of them is that "idh" accompanies, in the predominant usage of the speech of the Arabs among themselves, the past tense of the verb, even though they do sometimes bring it in in the position of a report about what will happen, when the hearers know its meaning. But that is not widespread, nor eloquent in their speech; and directing the meanings of the speech of God, Exalted is He, to what is better known and more familiar, so long as a way to that is found, is preferable to directing them to what is less known and more obscure.

- The other is that neither Jesus nor any of the prophets was in doubt that God does not forgive a polytheist who dies in his polytheism, such that it could be imagined of Jesus that he would say in the Hereafter, answering his Lord, Exalted be His mention: If You punish those who took me and my mother as two gods besides You, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise.
If someone says: What was the point of God's asking Jesus, "did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?", when He knew that Jesus had not said that?

It is said: That admits of two aspects of interpretation. One of them: warning Jesus against saying that, and forbidding him, as a speaker says to another, "Did you do such-and-such?" concerning something of which the one addressed knows that the speaker regards the doing of what he said to him "did you do it?" as grave, by way of forbidding him to do it and threatening him over it.

The other: informing him that his people, whom he had left, had violated his covenant and changed their religion after him. He would thereby combine informing him of their state after him with warning him against saying it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the interpretation of the speech, it is: Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods, that is, two objects of worship whom you worship besides God? Jesus said: I declare You, O Lord, far above, and too exalted, for me to do that or to speak it; "it is not for me to say what I have no right to", he says: it is not for me to say that, because I am a created servant, and my mother is Your handmaid; and how could a servant and a handmaid lay claim to lordship? "If I had said it, You would have known it", he says: nothing is hidden from You, and You know that I did not say that nor command them to it.
### On the interpretation of His words: You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your self. Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen things (5:116)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He, Exalted be His mention, says, reporting about His prophet Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him): that he declares himself before Him innocent of what the unbelievers among the Christians said about him and about his mother, that he should have called them to it or commanded them to it; so he said: "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it." Then he said: "You know what is in my self", he says: O Lord, what my self has concealed, which I have not uttered nor manifested with my limbs, is not hidden from You; how much less, then, what I have uttered and manifested with my limbs? He says: had I said to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God", You would have known it, because You know the secret thoughts of souls which they have not uttered; how much more what has been uttered? "And I do not know what is in Your self", he says: and I do not know what You have hidden from me and not acquainted me with, because I know of things only what You have made known to me; "indeed You are the Knower of the unseen things", he says: You are the One who knows the hidden matters on which none but You is informed, and which none other than You knows.

### On the interpretation of His words: I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them so long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are witness over all things (5:117)

Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a report from God, Exalted be His mention, about the words of Jesus. He says: I said to them nothing except that speech which You commanded me to say to them, namely that I said to them, "Worship God, my Lord and your Lord"; "and I was a witness over them so long as I was among them", he says: and I was, regarding what they did while I was in their midst, a witness over them and over their deeds and their words; "but when You took me up" (tawaffaytanī), he says: but when You took me to Yourself; "You were the Watcher over them", he says: You were the Guardian over them, rather than I, because I witnessed of their deeds only what they did while I was in their midst.

In this is a clarification that God, Exalted be His mention, made the deeds of the people and their saying known to him only after He had taken him to Himself and taken him up, by His words, "did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"

"And You are witness over all things", he says: and You witness all things, because nothing is hidden from You; as for me, I witnessed only some things, namely what I saw with my own eyes while I was dwelling in the midst of the people; so I testify only to that which I saw with my own eyes, beheld and witnessed.
Something like what we have said about His words "You were the Watcher over them" was said by the people of interpretation.
### Those who said this

(13032) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to me: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: You were the Watcher over them: as for "the Watcher" (al-raqīb), it is the Guardian.
(13033) Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: You were the Watcher over them: he said: the Guardian.

A group of the people of knowledge used to say: The answer with which Jesus answered his Lord was from God, Exalted is He, an instruction (tawqīf) from Him to him in it.{{fn:That is, God Himself taught Jesus the words of his reply; he did not compose them of his own accord.}}
### Those who said this

(13034) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Ibn Yamān related to us, from Sufyān, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father: Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to: he said: God instructed him in it.

(13035) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī related to us: it was read before Sufyān, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father Ṭāwūs, who said: Jesus argued his case, and God instructed him in it: Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?, the verse.

(13036) Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: Jarīr related to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Maysarah, who said: God, Exalted be His mention, said: O Jesus, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He said: And his joints trembled, and he feared that he might have said it, and he said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your self. Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen things.
### On the interpretation of His words: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise (5:118)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He, Exalted be His mention, says: If You punish these people who uttered this saying, by causing them to die upon it, they are Your servants, submissive to You, unable to withhold themselves from what You intend for them, and unable to ward off from themselves any harm or any decree by which You reach them; and if You forgive them, by Your guiding them to repentance from it, so that You cover it over for them, You are indeed the Mighty in His vengeance upon whomever He wishes to take vengeance, none being able to ward Him off from him; the Wise in His guiding of those of His creatures whom He has guided to repentance, and in His granting success to those of them whom He has granted success in finding the path of deliverance from punishment; as in that which:

(13037) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His words If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them: by bringing them out of Christianity and guiding them to Islam, You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise. And this is the saying of Jesus in this world.

(13038) al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise, he said: By God, they were not given to reviling nor to cursing.{{fn:That is, the prophets did not curse or revile their peoples but referred their affair to God, as Jesus does here.}}

### On the interpretation of His words: God said: This is a day when the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein for ever (5:119)

Abū Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the reading of His words This is a day when the truthful shall profit. Some of the people of the Ḥijāz and Medina read it hādhā yawma yanfaʿu al-ṣādiqīn, with "day" (yawm) in the accusative.

Some of the people of the Ḥijāz and some of the people of Medina, and the generality of the reciters of the people of Iraq, read it hādhā yawmu yanfaʿu al-ṣādiqīn, with "day" in the nominative. Whoever put it in the nominative did so by making it the predicate of "this" (hādhā), and treated "day" as a noun, even though its annexation (iḍāfa) is not a pure one, because it has become like a noun that is qualified.

Some of the grammarians used to claim that the Arabs, in the inflection of time-words such as "day" and "night", treat them as they treat what comes after them. If what comes after them is nominative, they put them in the nominative, as in their saying hādhā yawmu yarkabu al-amīr (this is the day the commander rides out), laylatu yaṣduru al-ḥājj (the night the pilgrims set forth), and yawmu akhūka munṭaliq (the day your brother departs). And if what comes after them is accusative, they put them in the accusative, as in their saying hādhā yawma kharaja al-jaysh wa-sāra al-nās (this is the day the army went out and the people marched), and laylata qutila Zayd (the night Zayd was killed), and the like of that, even though their meaning in both cases is "when" (idh and idhā).
It seems that whoever read it thus, in the nominative, directed the speech to its being among what God will say on the Day of Resurrection.
Likewise al-Suddī used to say regarding that.

(13039) Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to me: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: God said: This is a day when the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness. This is a break from the speech of Jesus, and this is the Day of Resurrection.

By his saying "this is a break from the speech of Jesus" al-Suddī means that His words Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to up to His words You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise (5:116–118) are part of God's report, Mighty and Majestic, about Jesus, that he said it in this world after He had raised him to Himself, and that what comes after that is God's speech to His servants on the Day of Resurrection.
As for the accusative in this, it may be construed in two ways:

- One of them is that the annexation of "day" to anything other than a noun makes it accusative, because the annexation is not pure; the annexation is pure only when it is annexed to a true noun. The counterparts of "day" in this respect are "time" (ḥīn) and "season" (zamān) and the like of them among the words for time, as al-Nābighah{{fn:Al-Nābighah al-Dhubyānī, the pre-Islamic poet; the verse is from his ode of apology to al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir.}} said:
> At the time when I reproached grey hairs for youthful folly,
> and said: Have you not yet come to your senses, when hoariness is a restrainer?

- The other way is that what is intended by the speech is: this matter and this affair is on the day the truthful shall profit; so "the day" would then be accusative as an adverb of time and a qualifier, with the meaning: this matter is on a day when the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this, in my view, is hādhā yawma yanfaʿu al-ṣādiqīn, with "the day" in the accusative, on the basis that it is accusative as an adverb of time and a qualifier. For the meaning of the speech is: God, Majestic and Exalted be His mention, answered Jesus when he said Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it up to His words You are indeed the Mighty, the Wise (5:116–118), and He, Mighty and Majestic, said to him: This beneficial saying, or this beneficial truthfulness, is on the day when the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness. So "the day" is the time of the beneficial saying and truthfulness.
If someone should say: What then is the syntactic position of "this"? It is said: nominative.

If he should say: Then where is that which governs it in the nominative? It is said: it is implied. It is as if He said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: This; this is a day when the truthful shall profit from their truthfulness; as the poet said:
> Do you not see the clouds, how they run?
> This, and not your horses, O Ibn Bishr!
He means: this is this, and not your horses.

Abū Jaʿfar said: So the interpretation of the speech, since the matter is as we have described for the reasons we have set out, is: God said to Jesus: This beneficial saying is on a day when those who were truthful in this world shall profit from that truthfulness of theirs, in the Hereafter, with God; for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, He says: for those who were truthful in this world there are gardens beneath which rivers flow in the Hereafter, as a reward for them from God, Mighty and Majestic, for the truthfulness they showed, in that they were true to God in what they promised Him and fulfilled it for God, so God, Mighty and Majestic, fulfilled for them what He had promised them of His reward; abiding therein for ever, He says: remaining in the gardens which He has given them, for ever: perpetually, having therein a bliss which will not pass from them nor cease.
We have already explained previously that the meaning of "abiding" (khulūd) is perpetuity and permanence.
### On the interpretation of His words: God is well pleased with them and they are well pleased with Him. That is the great triumph (5:119)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He, Exalted be His mention, says: God is well pleased with these truthful ones, who were true in fulfilling for Him what they promised Him, of acting in obedience to Him and avoiding disobedience to Him; and they are well pleased with Him, He says: and they, for their part, are well pleased with God, Exalted be His mention, for His fulfilling for them what He promised them for their obedience to Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, of His abundant reward; that is the great triumph, He says: this which God has given them, of gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, He being pleased with them and they being pleased with their Lord, is the great attainment of the thing sought, and the achieving of the need which they used to seek in this world and for which they used to labour in it; so they obtained what they sought and achieved what they hoped for.
### On the interpretation of His words: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He has power over all things (5:120)

Abū Jaʿfar said: He, Exalted be His mention, says: O Christians, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, He says: His is the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, not Jesus, whom you claim to be your god, nor his mother, nor any of those who are in the heavens and those who are in the earth; for the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them are a creation of His creating, and Jesus and his mother are part of that, by their occupying place and passing from place to place; by their being in the place in which they are, through dwelling in it and moving from it, the two of them give proof that they are two servants, owned by Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He thereby alerts them, and all His creatures, to the point of His proof against them, that they may ponder it and take heed of it, and so understand from Him; and He has power over all things, He, Exalted be His mention, says: and God, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, is able to bring them to nought and to destroy them, and to destroy Jesus and his mother and all who are on the earth together, just as He originated their creation; that does not render Him incapable, nor does anything He wills, because His power is the power which no power resembles, and His sovereignty is the sovereignty which no sovereignty or kingdom resembles.
End of the commentary on Sūrat al-Māʾidah.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place, (16) and took a screen apart from them. Then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared to her as a well-formed human being (17) (19:16–17)

He, Exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): And mention, O Muḥammad, in the Book of God which He sent down to you with the truth, Mary daughter of ʿImrān, when she went apart from her people and secluded herself from them. It (intabadhat) is the iftaʿala form from nabdh, and nabdh means casting away; we have already explained that, with its evidential citations, previously.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words And mention in the Book Mary, when she withdrew, that is: she secluded herself from her people.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt related to us: Abū Kudaynah related to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place, he said: she went out to an eastern place.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: Mary went out to the side of the sanctuary (miḥrāb) because of a menstruation that had come upon her, and that is His words "and she withdrew from her people to an eastern place": in the eastern part of the sanctuary.
His words to an eastern place: He says: she moved away and went apart from her people to a spot towards the rising of the sun rather than its setting.
As in:
al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words an eastern place, he said: towards the east.

Isḥāq ibn Shāhīn related to me: Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: I am indeed the one of God's creatures who knows best why the Christians took the east as their direction of prayer (qibla): it is because of God's words "and she withdrew from her people to an eastern place"; so they took the birthplace of Jesus as their direction of prayer.
Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me: Dāwūd related to us, from ʿĀmir, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt informed us: Abū Kudaynah related to us, from Qābūs, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Prayer towards the House and pilgrimage to God were prescribed for the People of the Book, and nothing turned them away from these two except their interpretation of your Lord's words when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place; so they prayed towards the rising-place of the sun.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: when she withdrew from her people to an eastern place, he said: far off and set apart.

It was said that she went to a place adjoining the rising of the sun only because what lies towards the east was, in their view, better than what lies towards the west; and so too is this, according to what is reported, among the Arabs.

His words and took a screen apart from them: He says: she took, apart from her people, a covering that would screen her from them and from the people. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that she went to a place adjoining the east because God shaded her with the sun and made of it a screen for her.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words she withdrew from her people to an eastern place, he said: a place where the sun shaded her, so that none of them should see her.
Others said about it what:
Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: and took a screen apart from them: of walls.

His words Then We sent to her Our Spirit: He, Exalted be His mention, says: Then We sent to her, when she had withdrawn from her people to an eastern place and taken a screen apart from them, Gabriel.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words Then We sent to her Our Spirit, he said: He sent to her, according to what has been related to us, Gabriel.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: She found with her Gabriel, whom God had given the likeness of a well-formed human being.
al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words Then We sent to her Our Spirit, he said: Gabriel.

Muḥammad ibn Sahl related to me: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb, related to me, saying: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: God sent Gabriel to Mary, and he appeared to her as a well-formed human being.

Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When she became pure, meaning Mary, from her menstruation, there was a man with her; and that is His words Then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared to her as a well-formed human being. He, Exalted be His mention, says: he took on for her the likeness of a human being of sound form among them, meaning in the form of a man of the sons of Adam, of well-proportioned build.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: She said: I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing. (18) He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, to bestow on you a pure boy (19) (19:18–19)
He, Exalted be His mention, says: Mary was afraid of Our messenger when he appeared to her as a well-formed human being, and she thought him a man who desired her for himself.

al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing, he said: She feared that he only desired her for himself.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: and he appeared to her as a well-formed human being: when she saw him she was frightened of him and said I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing.

So she said: I take refuge, O man, in the All-Merciful from you; she means: I seek protection in the All-Merciful from you, lest you obtain from me what He has forbidden to you, if you are one who fears Him, who guards against what He has made inviolable and avoids disobedience to Him; for whoever is God-fearing avoids that. And if this were construed as her meaning: I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you fear God with respect to my seeking protection and refuge in Him from you, that would be a sound construction.
As in:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: She said: I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing, she supposing him to be nothing other than a man of the sons of Adam.

Abū Kurayb related to us: Abū Bakr related to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: Ibn Zayd said, and he mentioned the story of Mary, and said: She knew that the God-fearing man is a man of restraint when she said I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing. He said: I am only a messenger of your Lord. He, Exalted be His mention, says: So Our Spirit said to her: I am only a messenger of your Lord, O Mary; He has sent me to you to bestow on you a pure boy.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Iraq, other than Abū ʿAmr, read it li-ahaba laki ("that I may bestow on you"), with the meaning: I am only a messenger of your Lord; he says: He has sent me to you that I may bestow on you a pure boy, as a report of his words. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read it li-yahaba laki ghulāman zakiyyan ("that He may bestow on you a pure boy"), with the meaning: I am only a messenger of your Lord; He has sent me to you that God may bestow on you a pure boy.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this is that upon which the reciters of the garrison cities agree, which is li-ahaba laki, with the alif rather than the yāʾ, because it is so in the codices (maṣāḥif) of the Muslims, and upon it is the reading of their early and their later ones, apart from Abū ʿAmr; and it is not permissible to oppose them in what they have agreed upon, nor is it allowable for anyone to oppose their codices. The "pure" boy is one who is pure of sins; and so the Arabs say ghulām zākin and zakiyy, and ʿālin and ʿaliyy.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: She said: How can I have a boy, when no human being has touched me, and I have not been unchaste? (20) He said: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me; and that We may make him a sign for mankind and a mercy from Us; and it is a matter decreed (21) (19:20–21)

He, Exalted be His mention, says: Mary said to Gabriel How can I have a boy: from what quarter shall I have a boy? Is it from a husband whom I marry, so that I am granted him from him, or will God originate his creation in me from nothing? when no human being has touched me of the children of Adam by lawful marriage, and I have not been, since none of them has touched me in the lawful way, unchaste: I have not acted unchastely and done that in the unlawful way, so as to have conceived him by fornication.
As in:

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: and I have not been unchaste, he says: a fornicatress. He said: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me: He, Exalted be His mention, says: Gabriel said to her: The matter is thus, as you describe, in that no human being has touched you and you have not been unchaste; but your Lord has said: It is easy for Me, that is: the creation of the boy whom I said I would bestow upon you is easy for Me; his creation, and his bestowal upon you without a male to impregnate you, is not difficult for Me.

and that We may make him a sign for mankind: He says: and so that We may make the boy whom We bestow upon you a token and a proof against My creatures, I bestow him upon you. and a mercy from Us: He says: and as a mercy from Us to you and to whoever believes in him and affirms him, I create him from you. and it is a matter decreed: He says: and his creation from you was a matter which God had decreed, and which had passed in His judgement and His prior knowledge, that it would come to be from you.
As in:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, who said: one whom I do not suspect related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: and it is a matter decreed, that is: God has resolved upon that, so there is no escaping it.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a far-off place. (22) Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm-tree. She said: Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind! (23) (19:22–23)

In this speech there is something left out, omitted from mention because what is mentioned of it suffices to indicate it: "So We breathed into her of Our Spirit, with a boy, so she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a far-off place." And so the interpretation of the people of interpretation has come.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Sahl related to me: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil, the nephew of Wahb ibn Munabbih, related to me, saying: I heard Wahb say: When God sent Gabriel to Mary, he appeared to her as a well-formed human being, and she said to him I take refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing; then he breathed into the neck-opening of her shift, until the breath reached the womb, and she conceived.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamānī, who said: When he said that, meaning when Gabriel said He said: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me, to the end of the verse, she submitted to the command of God, and he breathed into the opening of her garment, then departed from her.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: She threw her outer wrap over herself when Gabriel said that to her, and Gabriel took hold of her two sleeves and breathed into the neck-opening of her shift, which was slit at the front; the breath entered her breast and she conceived. Then her sister, the wife of Zachariah, came to her one night to visit her, and when she opened the door to her she embraced her, and the wife of Zachariah said: "O Mary, do you know that I am pregnant?" Mary said: "And do you know that I too am pregnant?" The wife of Zachariah said: "I find that what is in my belly prostrates to what is in your belly." And that is His words confirming a word from God (3:39).
al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: They say that he breathed only into the neck-opening of her shift and her sleeve.

His words and withdrew with him to a far-off place: He says: she went apart with the one she had conceived, namely Jesus, and withdrew with him from the people to a far-off place; He says: a remote place, distant from the people. One says: he is in a place that is qāṣin, and qaṣiyy, with one and the same meaning, as the rajaz-poet{{fn:Ruʾbah ibn al-ʿAjjāj, the Umayyad-era master of the rajaz metre.}} said:
> You shall surely sit in the seat of one far removed
> from me, a man of foul ways, detested.
From it one says qaṣā al-makānu yaqṣū quṣuwwan, when it is far off; and aqṣaytu al-shayʾa, when you have put a thing far away and set it back.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words and withdrew with him to a far-off place, he said: a remote place.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words a far-off place, he said: distant.
al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When the time came for Mary to give birth, she went out to the eastern side of the sanctuary and came to its furthest part.

His words Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm-tree: He, Exalted be His mention, says: the labour pains brought her to the trunk of the palm-tree. Then it was said that when the bāʾ was dropped from it, it became ajāʾahā, just as one says ataytuka bi-Zayd ("I came to you with Zayd"), and when you drop the bāʾ it is said ātaytuka Zaydan ("I brought you Zayd"), as He, Majestic is His praise, said Bring me pieces of iron (18:96), the meaning being "come to me with pieces of iron", except that the alif was lengthened when the bāʾ was dropped; and as they said kharajtu bihi and akhrajtuhu ("I went out with it" and "I brought it out"), and dhahabtu bihi and adhhabtuhu ("I went off with it" and "I took it away"). It is simply the afʿala form from majīʾ (coming), as one says jāʾa huwa ("he came") and ajaʾtuhu anā ("I made him come"), that is, I brought him. Among the proverbs of the Arabs is: "It is an evil thing that has driven me (ajāʾanī) to the marrow of a hock",{{fn:The hock has no marrow; only one in utter want would resort to it, so the proverb is said of being driven by necessity to what is worthless.}} and also ashāʾa; it is said: "an evil thing it is that drives you (yujīʾuka) and forces you (yushīʾuka) to that"; and from this is the saying of Zuhayr:{{fn:Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā, the pre-Islamic poet.}}
> And many a protégé who journeyed, making straight for you,
> whom fear and hope together drove on.

He means: brought him, and drove him to us. Ashāʾaka is of the dialect of Tamīm, and ajāʾaka of the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliyah.{{fn:The highlands around Medina and the Ḥijāz, whose Arabic the grammarians often cite.}} Those who interpreted it with the meaning "compelled her" (aljaʾahā) did so only because when the labour pains brought her to the trunk of the palm-tree, they had thereby compelled her to it.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words Then the pangs of childbirth drove her, he said: the labour pains compelled her.

al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: the labour pains compelled her. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ibn ʿAbbās said: the labour pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm-tree.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm-tree, he says: the labour pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm-tree.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, concerning His words Then the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of the palm-tree, he said: they forced her to the trunk of the palm-tree.
They differed as to which was the place to which Mary withdrew with Jesus to give birth to him, and to which the labour pains drove her.

- Some of them said: That was in the nearest part of the land of Egypt and the furthest part of the land of Syria; for she fled from her people when she conceived and set out towards Egypt, fleeing from them.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Sahl related to us: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil related to me that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Mary conceived, there was with her a kinsman of hers called Joseph the Carpenter, and the two of them used to go to the temple which is by Mount Zion; that temple was in those days among the greatest of their places of worship. Mary and Joseph used to serve in that temple at that time, and its service carried great merit, so they were eager for it, and they used to undertake its upkeep with their own hands: its adornment, its sweeping and its purification, and every work that was done in it; and none of the people of their time worked more strenuously or more devoutly than those two. The first to notice Mary's pregnancy was her companion Joseph. When he saw what was with her he found it monstrous; it weighed heavily upon him and he was appalled by it, and he did not know on what footing to place her affair. Whenever Joseph wished to suspect her, he remembered her righteousness and her innocence, and that she had never been absent from him for a single hour; and whenever he wished to acquit her, he saw what had appeared upon her. When this became too hard for him he spoke to her, and the first of his speech to her was that he said to her: "There has arisen in my mind concerning you a matter which I have feared; I have been anxious to kill it and conceal it within myself, but it has overcome me, and I have found that speaking of it is more healing for my breast." She said: "Then say a fair word." He said: "I would say to you nothing but that. So tell me: does a crop grow without seed?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Does a tree grow without rain falling upon it?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Can there be a child without a male?" She said: "Yes. Do you not know that God, Blessed and Exalted, made the crop grow on the day He created it without seed, and that seed on that day came only from the crop which God had made grow without seed? Or do you not know that God by His power made the trees grow without rain, and that by that same power He made rain the life of the trees after He had created each one of them separately? Or do you say that God was not able to make the trees grow until He sought the help of water for it, and that had it not been for that He would not have been able to make them grow?" Joseph said to her: "I do not say this; but I know that God, Blessed and Exalted, by His power over whatever He wills, says to it 'Be', and it is." Mary said: "Or do you not know that God, Blessed and Exalted, created Adam and his wife without female or male?" He said: "Indeed yes." When she said that to him, it fell into his mind that what was with her was something from God, Blessed and Exalted, and that it was not for him to question her about it, because of what he saw of her keeping it concealed. Then Joseph took over the service of the temple and spared her every work she used to do in it, because of what he saw of the thinness of her body, the yellowness of her complexion, the blotching of her face, the swelling of her belly, the weakness of her strength and the constant fixedness of her gaze; and Mary had not been like that before. When her confinement drew near, God revealed to her: Go out from the land of your people, for if they lay hold of you they will reproach you and kill your child. So she confided that to her sister, and her sister at that time was pregnant, having been given the glad tidings of John; and when the two met, the mother of John felt what was in her belly fall down upon its face in prostration, acknowledging Jesus. So Joseph carried her towards the land of Egypt on a donkey of his, there being nothing between her, when she mounted, and the pack-saddle. Joseph went on with her until, when he was on the border of the land of Egypt, at the furthest limit of the country of her people, the birth-pangs overtook Mary and compelled her to a donkey's manger, meaning the donkey's feeding-trough, and the foot of a palm-tree; and that was in a season which, I think, was cold, or hot (the doubt is from Abū Jaʿfar). The labour pains became severe for Mary, and when she felt their severity she took refuge at the palm-tree and clasped it, and the angels surrounded her, standing in rows encircling her.
Another opinion, other than this, has been related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, namely what:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When her delivery drew near, meaning Mary, and she felt what a woman feels of the pangs of labour, she went out of the city, departing from Aelia,{{fn:Īliyāʾ, the Arabic name for Jerusalem, from Aelia Capitolina.}} so that the birth should overtake her at a village six miles from Aelia called Bethlehem; and the labour pains drove her to the foot of a palm-tree, beside which was a cow's manger, and beneath it a spring of water; and she gave birth to him there.

- Others said: Rather, when the time came for her to deliver what was in her belly, she went out to the eastern side of the sanctuary and came to its furthest part, and the labour pains compelled her to the trunk of the palm-tree. That is the opinion of al-Suddī, and I have already mentioned the report of it before.

Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah related to me: Ḥajjāj related to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: al-Mughīrah ibn ʿUthmān informed me, saying: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: It was nothing but that she conceived and gave birth.

al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: And al-Mughīrah ibn ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: It was no more than that she conceived and gave birth.
His words Would that I had died before this: It is mentioned that she said that while in the pangs of labour, out of shame before the people.
As in:

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: She said, while in the pangs of labour from the pregnancy, out of shame before the people: Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind!

She says: would that I had died before this distress in which I am, and the grief of my giving birth to a child without a husband, and been a thing forgotten, out of mind (nasyan mansiyyan): something forgotten, the seeking of which has been abandoned, like the menstrual rags which, once thrown away and discarded, are neither sought nor remembered; and likewise everything that is forgotten and abandoned and not sought is a nasy. Nasy, with fatḥa on the nūn and with kasra, are two well-known dialectal forms among the dialects of the Arabs with a single meaning, like watr and witr, and jasr and jisr; and whichever of the two the reciter reads, he is correct in our view. With kasra the generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz, Medina and Baṣra, and some of the people of Kūfa, read it; and with fatḥa the people of Kūfa read it. From this is the saying of the poet:{{fn:Al-Shanfarā, the pre-Islamic outlaw-poet; the verse describes a modest woman who walks with her eyes on the ground as though tracing a thing she had lost.}}
> As though she had upon the ground some forgotten thing she was tracking
> whenever she went forth in the morning; and if she speaks to you, she speaks fair and true.

By his saying taquṣṣuhu he means: she seeks it, because she had forgotten it until it was lost, then remembered it and sought it; and by his saying tablit he means: she speaks well and truthfully. And if nasy were construed as the verbal noun of nisyān (forgetting), that would be correct, because the Arabs, according to what is reported of them, say nasītuhu nisyānan and nasyan, just as one of them said "of obedience to the Lord and disobedience (ʿaṣy) of Satan", meaning ʿiṣyān; and as you say ataytuhu ityānan and atyan, as the poet said:
> The committing of abominations among them is a thing well known,
> while they deem the doing of noble deeds forbidden.
His words out of mind (mansiyyan): a passive participle from nasītu al-shayʾa ("I forgot the thing"); it is as if she said: Would that I were the thing that is cast away, abandoned and forgotten.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind: I had not been created, and had not been anything.

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: and been a thing forgotten, out of mind, he says: nasyan: my mention forgotten; and mansiyyan, she says: my trace forgotten, so that neither trace nor substance of me is seen.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: and been a thing forgotten, out of mind: that is, something neither known nor remembered.

al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words and been a thing forgotten, out of mind, he said: I not being known, nor it being known who I am.
al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: a thing forgotten, out of mind, he said: it is the miscarried foetus.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind: I had never been anything on the earth at all.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: Then he called to her from beneath her: Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream. (24) And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates. (25) (19:24-25)

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Iraq read it fa-nādāhā min taḥtihā, then he called to her from beneath her, meaning: then Gabriel called to her from in front of her, though they differed among themselves in its interpretation: some of them, when reading it min taḥtihā in that way, interpreted it thus, while some of them interpreted it to mean that it was Jesus, and that he called to her from beneath her after she had given birth to him. Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it fa-nādāhā man taḥtahā, with the vowel a on both tāʾs of taḥt,{{fn:That is, the reading man taḥtahā, "the one who was beneath her", with a on man and on the final letter of taḥta, as against min taḥtihā, "from beneath her", with i.}} meaning: then the one who was beneath her called to her, on the basis that the one beneath her was Jesus, and that it was he who called to his mother.
### Those who said: the one who called to her from beneath her was the angel
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite then he called to her from beneath her, meaning: Gabriel.
Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh Aḥmad ibn Yūnus related to me: ʿAbthar informed us: Ḥuṣayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, who said: The one who called to her was the angel.

Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū Aḥmad related to us: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, that he recited: then he addressed her from beneath her (fa-khāṭabahā min taḥtihā).
Abū Hishām al-Rifāʿī related to us: Yaḥyā related to us: Sufyān related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, that he recited: then he addressed her from beneath her.
Al-Rifāʿī related to us: Wakīʿ related to us, from his father, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, that he recited it thus.
Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀmir related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: then he called to her from beneath her: he said: Gabriel.
Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, from Sufyān, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the like of it.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: then he called to her from beneath her: that is, from beneath the palm tree.
Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: then he called to her, Gabriel, from beneath her: Do not grieve.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words then he called to her from beneath her: he said: the angel.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words then he called to her from beneath her: meaning: Gabriel; he was lower down than she was.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: then he called to her from beneath her: he said: Gabriel called to her, and Jesus did not speak until she came to her people.
### Those who said: Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) called to her
Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His words then he called to her from beneath her: he said: Jesus son of Mary.
Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀmir related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
