Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: then he called to her from beneath her: her son.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, who said: al-Ḥasan said: It is her son.
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: then he called to her, Jesus, from beneath her: Do not grieve.

Abū Ḥumayd Aḥmad ibn al-Mughīrah al-Ḥimṣī related to me: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to us, from Thābit ibn ʿAjlān, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, on His words then he called to her from beneath her: he said: Jesus. Do you not hear God say then she pointed to him (19:29)?

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: then he called to her from beneath her: he said: Jesus; he called to her from beneath her: Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream.

I was told on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah al-Riyāḥī, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The one who addressed her was the one whom she had carried in her womb and who had entered by way of her mouth.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more fitting of the two opinions on this, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: the one who called to her was her son Jesus. That is because, of the pronouns that refer to him, this one is nearer to the mention of him than it is to the mention of Gabriel, and referring it back to that which is nearer to it is more fitting than referring it back to that which is further from it. Do you not see that in the sequence of His words So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a far-off place (19:22), by which He means: so she conceived Jesus and withdrew with him, it is then said: then he called to her, following on in order from that mention of Jesus and the account of him? And for another reason, namely His words then she pointed to him (19:29): she would not have pointed to him, God willing, unless she already knew that he could speak in that condition of his, and on account of what she had come to know and to trust of him through his addressing her with his words to her, Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream, and through what God has related of him, that he said to her: point the people to him. Had that been a saying of Gabriel, it would have been fitting that there be, in the plain sense of the account, a clear statement that Jesus would speak and argue on her behalf before the people, and a command from Gabriel to her that she point the people to him when they asked her about her condition and his.

If that is the correct interpretation, as we have explained, then it is clear that both readings, I mean min taḥtihā with the vowel i and man taḥtahā with the vowel a, are correct. That is because when it is read with i, there is in His words then he called to her a pronoun referring to Jesus; and when man taḥtahā is read with a, the verb belongs to man, the one who, and that is Jesus. The interpretation of the words, then, is: then the newborn called to her from beneath her: do not grieve, O my mother; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream.
As in the following:

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words then he called to her from beneath her: Do not grieve: She said: How should I not grieve when you are with me, and I am neither a married woman, that I might say he is from a husband, nor a slave woman, that I might say he is from my master? What excuse have I before the people? Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind! (19:23). So Jesus said to her: I will spare you the speaking.
The people of interpretation differed over what is meant by the stream (sarī) in this place. Some of them said: by it is meant the small river.
### Those who said this
Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: Sufyān related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: the rivulet (jadwal).

Ibn Bashshār related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I heard al-Barāʾ say concerning this verse, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: the rivulet.
ʿAlī related to me: ʿAbd Allāh related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, on His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: and it is the river of Jesus.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, on His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: The sarī is the river that was beneath Mary when she gave birth to him; it was flowing, and it was called a sarī.

Abū Ḥuṣayn related to me: ʿAbthar related to us: Ḥuṣayn related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn al-Awdī, who said concerning this verse, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: The sarī is a river from which one drinks.

Yaʿqūb and Abū Kurayb related to us, both saying: Hushaym related to us: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, concerning His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: It is the rivulet.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: a stream: he said: a river, in Syriac.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it. Ibn Jurayj said: a river beside her.

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū Dāwūd related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: He was a sarī.{{fn:Al-Ḥasan here takes sarī in its other sense, "noble, eminent", as a description of Jesus; see the second opinion below.}} Then Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: The sarī is the rivulet. And he said: The commanders have got the better of us over you.

Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: he said: It is the rivulet, the small river; in Nabataean it is al-sarī.

Abū Ḥumayd al-Ḥimṣī related to me: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd related to us: Muḥammad ibn Muhājir related to us, from Thābit ibn ʿAjlān, who said: I asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr about the sarī, and he said: a river.
Abū Kurayb related to us: Hushaym related to us, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: the small river.

Yaʿqūb related to me: Hushaym related to us: Mughīrah informed us, from Ibrāhīm, that he said: It is the small river, meaning the rivulet; he means His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream.
Ibn Wakīʿ related to us: my father related to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayṭ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: a small rivulet, in Syriac.

It was related to us on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh, who said: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words beneath you a stream: the small rivulet among rivers.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: and the sarī is the rivulet; so the people of the Ḥijāz name it.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us: Maʿmar informed us, concerning His words a stream: he said: It is a rivulet.
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: meaning a channel of water.
Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: and the sarī is the river.
Others said: by it He meant Jesus.
### Those who said this
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: and the sarī is Jesus himself.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words your Lord has placed beneath you a stream: He means himself. He said: And what thing is more eminent (asrā) than he? He said: As for those who say that the sarī is the river, the river is not like that: had it been the river, it would only have been beside her, and a river is not beneath her.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more fitting of the two opinions on this, in my view, as regards correctness, is the opinion of those who said: by it He meant the rivulet. That is because he was informing her of what God had brought to her, of the water that He had placed by her, and he said to her, And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates. So eat, of these fresh dates, and drink, of this water, and be comforted (19:25-26), by your child. And the sarī is well known in the speech of the Arabs as the small river. From this is the saying of Labīd:{{fn:Labīd ibn Rabīʿah al-ʿĀmirī, the pre-Islamic poet and Companion; the line is from his Muʿallaqah, describing a wild ass and his mate coming down to water.}}
> So the two of them went into the midst of the breadth of the stream (sarī) and cleft
> a brimming pool, its rushes growing close together.
It is also transmitted as fīnā masjūrah, and it is also transmitted as fa-ghādarā, and the two left behind.
### His words: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree (19:25)
It is mentioned that the trunk was a dry trunk, and that he commanded her to shake it, this being in the days of winter; and her shaking it was her moving it.
As in the following:
Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: he said: move it.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: he said: It was a dry trunk, and he said to her: shake it, it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates.
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us, who said: I heard Abū Nahīk say: It was a dry palm tree.

Muḥammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar related to me: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Karīm related to us: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn Maʿqil related to me, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say concerning His words And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: and the fresh dates kept falling upon her, and that was in winter.

Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: it was a trunk cut off from the tree, and she shook it, and behold, it was a palm tree; and a river was made to flow for her in the sanctuary (miḥrāb), and the palm tree dropped fresh, ripe dates. Then he said to her, So eat and drink and be comforted (19:26).
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: and shake towards you the palm tree.
### Those who said this
Ibn Bashshār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Sufyān related to us, who said: Mujāhid said: And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: he said: the palm tree.

Ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū Aḥmad related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĪsā ibn Maymūn, from Mujāhid, concerning His words And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree: he said: the ʿajwah.{{fn:ʿAjwah is a prized variety of date palm, especially associated with Medina.}}

Yaʿqūb related to me: Hushaym related to us: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, that he recited this verse, And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates, and ʿAmr said: There is nothing better for a woman in childbed than dried dates and fresh dates.

The bāʾ was introduced in His words wa-huzzī ilayki bi-jidhʿ al-nakhlah, and shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, just as one says zawwajtuka fulānah and zawwajtuka bi-fulānah, I married you to so-and-so, and as He said tanbutu bi-l-duhn, it produces oil (23:20), meaning tanbutu al-duhn.

The Arabs only do that because verbs are alluded to by means of the bāʾ: when one alludes to I struck ʿAmr, one says faʿaltu bihi, I did it to him, and likewise with every verb. For that reason the bāʾ is introduced upon verbs and dropped from them, and its introduction and its omission bear one meaning. So the meaning of the words is: and shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree. And had the exegetes interpreted it as: and shake towards you fresh dates by the trunk of the palm tree, in the sense of: upon the trunk of the palm tree, that too would have been a sound construal; but I do not recall of anyone that he interpreted it so. Among the evidence for the bāʾ being introduced in a position where its introduction and its omission are alike is the saying of the poet:
> In a Yemeni valley whose upper part grows the lote tree,

> and its lower part the markh and the shabahān.{{fn:The markh is a desert tree whose wood kindles readily; the shabahān is a thorny shrub of the Yemen. The line is cited because bi-l-markh has the bāʾ where plain al-markh would mean the same.}}

The reciters differed over the reading of His words tassāqaṭ, it will drop. The generality of the reciters of Medina, Basra and Kufa read it tassāqaṭ, with a tāʾ, from tasāqaṭa, and with doubling of the sīn, meaning: the palm tree will drop (tatasāqaṭ) upon you fresh, ripe dates, one of the two tāʾs then being assimilated into the other so that it is doubled. It is as though those who read it thus directed the meaning of the words to: and shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, the palm tree will drop upon you fresh dates. Some of the reciters of Kufa read it tasāqaṭ, with a tāʾ and lightening of the sīn, and they directed the meaning of the words to the same as that to which those who doubled it directed it, except that they differed from them in the reading. And it is transmitted from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib that he read it yusāqiṭ, with a yāʾ.

Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf related that to me: al-Qāsim related to us: Yazīd related to us, from Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I heard al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib recite it thus. It is as though he directed the meaning of the words to: and shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree, the trunk will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates.
And it is transmitted from Abū Nahīk that he used to read it tusqiṭ, with the vowel u on the tāʾ and omission of the alif.

Ibn Ḥumayd related that to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us, who said: I heard Abū Nahīk recite it thus. It is as though he directed the meaning of the words to: the palm tree will let fall upon you fresh, ripe dates.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct opinion on this, in my view, is to say that these three readings, I mean tassāqaṭ with a tāʾ and doubling of the sīn, with a tāʾ and lightening of the sīn, and with a yāʾ and doubling of the sīn, are readings close to one another in meaning, each one of which has been read by reciters possessed of knowledge of the Qurʾān; so by whichever of them the reciter reads, he hits upon what is correct in it. That is because when the trunk drops fresh dates while it stands fixed and uncut, the palm tree has dropped fresh dates; and when the palm tree has dropped fresh dates, the palm tree in its entirety has dropped them, its trunk and what is other than its trunk. For as long as the palm tree stands upon its root, it is nothing but trunk, frond-stalks and fronds; it is when it is cut down that it becomes a trunk (jidhʿ). And as for the trunk which Mary was commanded to shake, no one we know of mentioned that it was a cut trunk except al-Suddī, and he claimed that through her shaking it, it became a palm tree once more. So his meaning and the meaning of those who said that what dropped fresh dates upon her was a palm tree have become one, and by that the soundness of what we have said is made clear.
### His words: ripe (janiyyan)

He means: gathered (majnī). Its original form was the pattern mafʿūl, and it was turned into the pattern faʿīl. The gathered (majnī) is that which is taken while fresh; and whatever is taken from a fruit tree, or moved from its place while still fresh, has been gathered (ujtuniya). For that reason it is said: so-and-so gathers (yajtanī) truffles. From this is the saying of the son of the sister of Jadhīmah:{{fn:ʿAmr ibn ʿAdī al-Lakhmī, nephew of the Lakhmid king Jadhīmah al-Abrash. Sent out with others to gather truffles for the king, he alone brought back the best of what he found instead of eating it, and said these words, which became a proverb for one who gives his companion the pick of what he has.}}
> This is my gathering, and the choicest of it is in it,
> whereas every gatherer's hand goes to his mouth.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: So eat and drink and be comforted; and if you see any human being, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, so I shall not speak today to any human. (26) (19:26)

He says, Exalted be His mention: So eat of the fresh dates that fall upon you, and drink of the water of the stream that your Lord has placed beneath you; fear neither hunger nor thirst. And be comforted (wa-qarrī ʿaynan, literally: be cool of eye): He says: be of good cheer and rejoice at your giving birth to me, and do not grieve. The eye (ʿaynan) is put in the accusative because it is the eye that is described as being cooled. The meaning of the words is in fact: and let your eye be cooled by your child; then the verb was transferred from the eye to the woman who is the possessor of the eye, and the eye was put in the accusative, since in the original sense, according to the explanation, the verb belonged to it. This is comparable to what was done in His words but if they are pleased, of their own soul, to remit to you any part of it (4:4), which is in fact: but if their souls are pleased for you.

And His words and he was straitened for them in capacity (11:77).{{fn:Ḍāqa bihim dharʿan, in which dharʿan, capacity, stands in the accusative in the same way as ʿaynan and nafsan in the examples just given.}}

And from this are His words yusāqiṭ ʿalayki ruṭaban janiyyan, it will drop upon you fresh, ripe dates (19:25): it is in fact: the fresh dates of the trunk will fall upon you, and then the verb was transferred to the trunk, in the reading of those who read it with a yāʾ. And in the reading of those who read tusāqiṭ with a tāʾ, its meaning is: the fresh dates of the palm tree will fall upon you, and then the verb was transferred to the palm tree.
The reciters differed over the reading of His words wa-qarrī, and be comforted.

As for the people of Medina, they read it wa-qarrī, with the vowel a on the qāf, according to the dialect of those who say qarirtu bi-l-makān aqarru bihi, I settled in the place, and qarirtu ʿaynan aqarru bihi qurūran, I was cooled of eye; this is the dialect of Quraysh, according to what has been mentioned to me, and upon it rests the reading.

As for the people of Najd, they say qarartu bihi ʿaynan aqirru bihi qarāran and qarartu bi-l-makān aqirru bihi; so the reading according to their dialect is wa-qirrī ʿaynan, with the vowel i on the qāf. The reading in our view is according to the dialect of Quraysh, with the vowel a on the qāf.
### His words: and if you see any human being (19:26)

He says: if you see any of the children of Adam speaking to you, or questioning you about anything of your affair and the affair of your child and the cause of your giving birth to him, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: He says: say: I have made obligatory upon myself, for God, a silence, that I shall not speak to any of the children of Adam today; so I shall not speak today to any human.
The like of what we have said concerning the meaning of the fast was said by the people of interpretation.
### Those who said this
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān related to us, from his father, who said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say concerning this verse, I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: a silence.

Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah related to me: Ḥajjāj related to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: al-Mughīrah ibn ʿUthmān informed me, who said: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: he said: a silence.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, on His words I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: he said: by the fast He means silence.

Yaʿqūb related to me: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Sulaymān al-Taymī, who said: I heard Anas recite: and I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast and a silence (wa-innī nadhartu li-l-Raḥmān ṣawman wa-ṣamtan).

Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: as for His words a fast, she fasted from food, drink and speech.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: he said: Among the Children of Israel there were those who, when they strove in devotion, would fast from speech as one fasts from food, except for the remembrance of God. So he said that to her, and she said: I am fasting from speech as I fast from food, except for the remembrance of God. So when they spoke to her, she pointed to him, and they said How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (19:29). And he answered them and said I am the servant of God; He has given me the Book (19:30), as far as That is Jesus son of Mary, the word of truth, concerning which they are in doubt (19:34).

They differed over the reason on account of which he commanded her to fast from speaking to human beings. Some of them said: he commanded her to do that because she had no manifest argument before the people, for she had come, being an unmarried woman, with a child; so she was commanded to refrain from speech, so that her child might suffice her in speaking.
### Those who said this

Hārūn ibn Isḥāq al-Hamdānī related to us: Muṣʿab ibn al-Miqdām related to us: Isrāʾīl related to us: Abū Isḥāq related to us, from Ḥārithah, who said: I was with Ibn Masʿūd when two men came; one of them gave the greeting of peace and the other did not. He said: What is the matter with you? His companions said: He has sworn that he will not speak to people today. ʿAbd Allāh said: Speak to people and greet them with peace; for that was a woman who knew that no one would believe her that she had conceived without a husband, meaning by that Mary (peace be upon her).

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: When Jesus said to Mary Do not grieve (19:24), she said: How should I not grieve when you are with me, and I am neither a married woman nor a slave woman? What excuse have I before the people? Would that I had died before this and been a thing forgotten, out of mind! (19:23). So Jesus said to her: I will spare you the speaking. And if you see any human being, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, so I shall not speak today to any human. He said: All of this is the speech of Jesus to his mother.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: And if you see any human being, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, so I shall not speak today to any human: for I shall spare you the speaking.
Others said: that was simply a sign for Mary and her son.
### Those who said this

Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast: he said: In some of the readings (ḥurūf): a silence. That is because you will not meet any ignorant woman who says: I have vowed, as Mary vowed, not to speak for a day until night. God only made that a sign for Mary and for her son, and it is not lawful for anyone to vow a day's silence until night.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah; he recited I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, and it used to be read in the first reading (al-ḥarf al-awwal): a silence; it was simply a sign that God sent for Mary and her son.

Others said: Rather, she was fasting on that day, and one who fasted in that age would fast from food, drink and speaking to people; so Mary was permitted this measure of speech on that day while she was fasting.
### Those who said this

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: And if you see any human being who speaks to you, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, so I shall not speak today to any human: whoever fasted in that age would not speak until evening; so it was said to her: do not add to this.
### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said: O Mary, you have done a monstrous thing. (27) (19:27)
He says, Exalted be His mention: When Jesus said that to his mother, her soul was set at rest, she submitted to the command of God, and she carried him until she brought him to her people.
As in the following:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: The anguish of the trial and the fear of people made her, meaning Mary, forget what she used to hear from the angels of the glad tidings of Jesus; until, when he spoke to her, meaning Jesus, and there came to her the confirmation of what God had promised her, she took him up and then came with him to her people.
And al-Suddī said about this what follows:

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When she gave birth to him, Satan went and informed the Children of Israel that Mary had given birth; so they came running and called her, and she brought him to her people, carrying him.
### His words: They said: O Mary, you have done a monstrous thing (19:27)

He says, Exalted be His mention: When they saw Mary, and saw with her the child to whom she had given birth, they said to her: O Mary, you have come with an astonishing matter and brought about a grave event. Everyone who does a deed and does it thoroughly and well has wrought it (farāhu), as the rajaz poet said:{{fn:The lines are ascribed to Zurārah ibn Ṣaʿb, addressing a woman of the Banū ʿĀmir. Daqal is the poorest grade of date, and ḥujrī refers to Ḥujr, a town of al-Yamāmah. To "work the mighty work" (yafrī al-fariyya) is to do something prodigious; the poet mocks her for making a great show over worthless dates.}}
> You have fed me poor dates of Ḥujr,
> and yet over them you used to work the mighty work.
The like of what we have said about this was said by the people of interpretation.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on the words of God, Exalted, monstrous: he said: grave.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, on His words you have done a monstrous thing: he said: grave.
Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: you have done a monstrous thing: he said: grave.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When they saw her, and saw him with her, they said: O Mary, you have done a monstrous thing: that is, an indecency beyond compare.
### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste. (28) (19:28)

The people of interpretation differed over the reason on account of which it was said to her: O sister of Aaron, and over who this Aaron was whom God mentioned, relating that they attributed Mary to him as his sister. Some of them said: it was said to her O sister of Aaron as an attribution by them of her to righteousness, because the righteous among them used to be named Aaron; and he is not Aaron the brother of Moses.
### Those who said this

Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words O sister of Aaron: he said: There was a righteous man among the Children of Israel named Aaron, and they likened her to him and said: O you who resemble Aaron in righteousness.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, on His words O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste: he said: She was of a household known for righteousness and not known for corruption. Among people there are those who are known for righteousness and beget offspring in it, and others who are known for corruption and beget offspring in it. Aaron was a righteous man, beloved among his kinsfolk; and he is not Aaron the brother of Moses, but another Aaron. He said: And it has been mentioned to us that on the day he died forty thousand followed his bier, all of them named Aaron, from the Children of Israel.

Yaʿqūb related to me: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Ṣadaqah, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: I was informed that Kaʿb said: As for His words O sister of Aaron, this is not Aaron the brother of Moses. He said: ʿĀʾishah said to him: You have lied. He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said it, then he knows best and is better informed; otherwise, I find between the two of them six hundred years. He said: So she fell silent.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words O sister of Aaron: he said: A name coincided with a name. How many nations there were between Aaron and the two of them, nations upon nations!

Abū Kurayb, Ibn al-Muthannā, Sufyān, Ibn Wakīʿ and Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, all saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs al-Awdī related to us, who said: I heard my father mention, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wāʾil, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent me to the people of Najrān, and they said to me: Do you not recite O sister of Aaron? I said: Yes indeed. And you know what interval there was between Jesus and Moses. So I returned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him, and he said: "Why did you not inform them that they used to name themselves after their prophets and the righteous who were before them?"

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: al-Ḥakam ibn Bashīr related to us: ʿAmr related to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wāʾil, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) sent me on one of his errands to the people of Najrān, and they said: Does your Prophet not claim that Aaron the brother of Mary is the brother of Moses? I did not know what to answer them until I returned to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "They used to name themselves with the names of those who were before them."

Some of them said: by him is meant Aaron the brother of Moses, and Mary was attributed to him as his sister because she was of his descendants; one says to a Tamīmī: O brother of Tamīm, and to a Muḍarī: O brother of Muḍar.
### Those who said this

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: O sister of Aaron: he said: She was of the descendants of Aaron the brother of Moses, and it is as you say: O brother of the Banū So-and-so.
Others said: Rather, that was a man among them who was dissolute and open in his dissoluteness, and they attributed her to him.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct opinion on this is what the report from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) which we have mentioned has brought: that she was attributed to a man of her people.
### His words: your father was not a man of evil (19:28)
He says: your father was not a man of evil who committed indecencies; nor was your mother unchaste: He says: nor was your mother a fornicatress.
As in the following:
Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: nor was your mother unchaste: he said: a fornicatress.

He said nor was your mother unchaste (baghiyyan), and did not say baghiyyah, because that is one of the things by which women are described to the exclusion of men, so it followed the course of imraʾah ḥāʾiḍ, a menstruating woman, and ṭāliq, a divorced woman. Some of them used to liken that to their saying milḥafah jadīd, a new wrapper, and imraʾah qatīl, a slain woman.
### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: Then she pointed to him. They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (29) (19:29)
He says, Exalted be His mention: When her people said that to her, she said to them what Jesus had commanded her to say to them, and then she pointed them to Jesus, that they should speak to him.
As in the following:

Mūsā related to us: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When they said to her your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (19:28), she said to them what God had commanded her; and when after that they pressed her to speak, she pointed to him, to Jesus.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, on His words then she pointed to him: he said: she bade them speak to him.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: then she pointed to him: he says: she pointed to him, that they should speak to him.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, on His words then she pointed to him: that they should speak to him.
### His words: They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (19:29)

He says, Exalted be His mention: her people said to her: How shall we speak to one who is found in the cradle? The verb kāna in His words one who is in the cradle, a child has the meaning of the complete verb, not that which requires a predicate.{{fn:That is, kāna here is the full verb meaning "to come to be, to exist", not the copula "to be" that links a subject to a predicate.}} It is similar in meaning to the kāna in His words Am I anything but a human being, a messenger? (17:93), the meaning of which is: am I anything but a human being, a messenger? and: was I found, or was I sent, as anything other? And as Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
> I urged on along it a noble she-camel of Arḥab,{{fn:Arḥab is a clan of Hamdān to which a famous breed of riding camels was attributed.}}
> when the colour of the night had become like black-dyed leather.
meaning: and it had become, or was found. And it is said that by the cradle in this place He meant the lap of his mother.
### Those who said this
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: one who is in the cradle, a child: and the cradle is the lap.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already explained the meaning of the cradle in what has preceded, with its evidences, and that dispenses with repeating it in this place.

### On the interpretation of His words: He said: I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet, (30) and He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving as long as I live (31) (19:30–31)

God, Exalted be His mention, says: When Mary's people said to her How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant? (19:29), and supposed that this was mockery of them on her part, Jesus spoke, answering on his mother's behalf: I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture. And when she pointed them to Jesus they had, according to what is related of them, become angry; as in:

Mūsā related to me: ʿAmr related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, who said: When she pointed them to Jesus they grew angry, and said: Her mocking of us, when she bids us speak to this infant, is harder upon us than her fornication. They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant? (19:29)

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant? (19:29) Then Jesus answered them on her behalf and said to them: I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet … to the end of the verse.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant? He said to them: I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet (19:29–30) — and he recited until he reached and He has not made me arrogant, wretched (19:32) — : then they said: This is indeed a mighty matter.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant? He said: I am the servant of God (19:29–30): Jesus did not speak except at that moment, when they said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, an infant?

As for His words He has given me the Scripture: should someone say, "Did He then give him the Scripture and revelation before he was created in his mother's womb?", the meaning of this is other than what he supposes. Its meaning is only: He decreed, on the day He decreed the affairs of His creation, that He would give me the Scripture; as in:

Bishr ibn Ādam related to me: al-Ḍaḥḥāk, meaning Ibn Makhlad, related to us, from Sufyān, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah: He has given me the Scripture, he said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture, in what had gone before.

Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: Sufyān informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture, he said: the decree.

Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words I am the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture, he said: He decreed that He would give me the Scripture.

As for His words and made me a prophet: I have already explained the meaning of "prophet" (nabī), the disagreement of those who differed about it, and the correct opinion on it in our view together with its evidences, earlier in this work, in a way that dispenses with repeating it here.
Mujāhid used to say, concerning the meaning of "prophet" alone, what:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: The prophet alone is the one who is spoken to and upon whom revelation comes down, but who is not sent.
As for His words and He has made me blessed: the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is, "and He has made me greatly beneficial".
### Those who said this

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād al-Ṭalḥī related to me: al-ʿAlāʾ related to us, from ʿĀʾishah the wife of Layth, from Layth, from Mujāhid: and He has made me blessed, he said: greatly beneficial.
Others said: his blessing was the enjoining of right and the forbidding of wrong.
### Those who said this

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Khunays al-Makhzūmī related to us, he said: I heard Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, client of Banū Makhzūm, say: A learned man met a learned man who was above him in knowledge, and said to him: May God have mercy on you — what of my knowledge should I make public? He said: The enjoining of right and the forbidding of wrong, for that is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets to His servants; and the jurists have agreed upon the words of God and He has made me blessed wherever I may be. It was asked: What was his blessing? He said: The enjoining of right and the forbidding of wrong wherever he was.
Others said: the meaning of this is, "He has made me a teacher of good".
### Those who said this
Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me: Sufyān related to us, concerning His words and He has made me blessed wherever I may be, he said: a teacher of good.
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Jarīr related to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, His words and He has made me blessed wherever I may be, he said: a teacher of good wherever I was.

As for His words and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving: He says, and He decreed that He would enjoin upon me prayer and alms-giving (zakāh), meaning the observance of the limits of prayer and its establishment according to what He made obligatory upon me. In "alms-giving" (zakāh) there are two possible meanings: one of them is the zakāh of property, that he should pay it; the other is the purification of the body from the defilement of sins, in which case its meaning would be: and He enjoined upon me the abandoning of sins and the avoidance of acts of disobedience.

As for His words as long as I live: He says, as long as I am alive and existent in this world. This makes clear that the meaning of zakāh in this place is the purification of the body from sins, because Jesus, God's blessings and peace be upon him, is described as one who used to store up nothing for the morrow, such that zakāh of property would have become due from him — unless the zakāh that was imposed upon him was the giving in charity of everything surplus to his sustenance, in which case that would be a sound interpretation.

### On the interpretation of His words: and dutiful towards my mother, and He has not made me arrogant, wretched. (32) And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised up alive (33) (19:32–33)

God, Exalted be His mention, says, informing of what Jesus said to the people: "and He has made me blessed and dutiful (barran)", that is, He has made me dutiful towards my mother. Al-barr is the same as al-bārr (the dutiful one); one says "he is barr towards his father" and "bārr towards him". The reciters of the garrison towns read this word with fatḥah on the bāʾ. And from Abū Nahīk there is related what:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us: ʿAbd al-Muʾmin related to us, from Abū Nahīk, that he read and dutifulness (birran) towards my mother{{fn:Abū Nahīk read birran, with kasrah on the bāʾ, "dutifulness", the verbal noun, instead of the standard barran, "dutiful".}} as part of the speech of Jesus (peace be upon him). Abū Nahīk said: He enjoined upon me prayer, alms-giving and dutifulness towards parents, just as He enjoined that upon me.

It is as if Abū Nahīk directed the interpretation of the passage so that His words and dutifulness towards my mother are part of Jesus's report of God's enjoining it upon him, just as His words and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving are part of his report of God's enjoining that upon him. On this view the accusative of "dutifulness" must be owing to the operation of "enjoined" upon it, because prayer and alms-giving, although in the genitive in wording, are in the sense of the accusative, since they are the objects of the verb.

As for His words and He has not made me arrogant, wretched: He says, and He has not made me haughty towards God in what He commanded me and forbade me, wretched; rather He made me submissive in obedience to Him and made me humble; as in:

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: It was mentioned to us that he — meaning Jesus — used to say: Ask me, for my heart is soft, and I am small in my own eyes — on account of the humility that God had given him.

And Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: and dutiful towards my mother, and He has not made me arrogant, wretched: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary bringing the dead to life and healing the one born blind and the leper, among the signs over which God had given him power and in which He had permitted him; and she said: Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breast from which you were suckled! And the prophet of God, the son of Mary, said in answer to her: Blessed is he who recites the Book of God and follows what is in it. And He has not made me arrogant, wretched.

Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr related to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wāqid Abū Rajāʾ, from one of the people of knowledge, who said: You will not find one undutiful to his parents without finding him arrogant and wretched; then he recited and dutiful towards my mother, and He has not made me arrogant, wretched. He said: And you will not find one who treats his slaves badly without finding him conceited and boastful; then he recited and those whom your right hands possess; indeed God does not love whoever is conceited and boastful (4:36).

As for His words And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised up alive: He says, and security from God is upon me against Satan and his hosts on the day I was born, lest they obtain from me what they obtain at birth from those who are born, by way of pricking them; and on the day I die, from the terror of what is to be beheld; and on the day I am raised up alive, the Day of Resurrection, lest the dread that befalls people when they witness the terrors of that Day should befall me; as in:

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised up alive, he said: He informs them, in the course of his account of himself, that he has no father, and that he will die and then be raised up alive. God, Blessed and Exalted, says: Such is Jesus son of Mary — the word of truth about which they are in doubt (19:34).
### On the interpretation of His words: Such is Jesus son of Mary — the word of truth about which they are in doubt (34) (19:34)

God, Exalted be His mention, says: This one whose description I have set forth to you, and whose story I have told you, concerning the matter of the boy whom Mary bore, is Jesus son of Mary; this description is his description and this account is his account; and it is the word of truth, meaning that this account which I have narrated to you is the word of truth, and the speech I have recited to you is the word of God and His account, not the account of any other, into which illusion and doubt, addition and diminution enter. It is as though God, Exalted be His mention, were saying: So say concerning Jesus, O people, this word of which God has informed you about him — not what the Jews said, who claimed that he was not born of lawful wedlock and that he was a lying sorcerer, nor what the Christians said, that he was a son to God; for God has not taken a son, nor does that befit Him.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, His words Such is Jesus son of Mary — the word of truth, he said: God is the Truth.

Yaḥyā ibn Ibrāhīm al-Masʿūdī related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, who said: They used to say of this word, in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh{{fn:ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, whose codex and reading were followed in Kūfah.}} — he said: about which they are in doubt — he said: the Word of God.

Were the interpretation of this directed to "Such is Jesus son of Mary, the true word (al-qawl al-ḥaqq)", in the sense "that is the true word", with the definite article then removed from "word" and the word placed in construct with "truth" — as it is said Indeed this is the truth of certainty (56:95), and as it is said the true promise which they were promised (46:16) — it would be a sound interpretation.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The generality of the reciters of the Ḥijāz and Iraq read it qawlu l-ḥaqq, with the nominative on "word", according to the meaning I have described, making it in its inflection follow "Jesus", as an attribute (naʿt) of him. But the matter of its inflection is not, in my view, as those said who claimed that it is nominative as an attribute of "Jesus" — unless the meaning of "word" (qawl) be "the Word" (kalimah), according to what we have mentioned from Ibrāhīm concerning his interpretation of it in that way; in that case it would be correct for it to be an attribute of "Jesus". Otherwise its nominative is, in my view, by virtue of an implied word, namely "this is the word of truth", as the beginning of a new sentence (ibtidāʾ). That is because the account of the story of Jesus and his mother has come to its end at His words Such is Jesus son of Mary; then He began a new report, that the truth in the matter of Jesus about which the nations dispute is this word of which God has informed His servants about him, and no other. ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read it with the accusative, and it is as though the two of them intended by that the verbal noun: "Such is Jesus son of Mary — a true saying (qawlan ḥaqqan)", and then the definite article was introduced into it. As for what is reported of Ibn Masʿūd, that he read "Such is Jesus son of Mary, qāl al-ḥaqq", it is in the sense of qawl al-ḥaqq, on the pattern of al-ʿāb and al-ʿayb (fault), and al-dhām and al-dhaym (blame).

Abū Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this, in our view, is the nominative, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. As for His words, Exalted be His mention, about which they are in doubt, He means: about which they contend and differ, from their saying "I disputed (māraytu) so-and-so", when you argue and contend with him.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, His words Such is Jesus son of Mary — the word of truth about which they are in doubt: The Jews and the Christians fell into doubt about him. As for the Jews, they claimed he was a lying sorcerer; as for the Christians, they claimed he was the son of God, and the third of three, and a god. All of them lied; rather he is the servant of God and His messenger, His Word and a spirit from Him.

Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, His words about which they are in doubt, he said: They differed. One party said: he is the servant of God and His prophet — and they believed in him. Another party said: nay, he is God. Another party said: he is the son of God — Blessed and Exalted is He, far above what they say. He said: That is His words Then the factions differed among themselves (19:37), and the verse in al-Zukhruf (43:65). He said: Diqyūs, Nasṭūr and Mār Yaʿqūb{{fn:The eponyms, as the early narrators knew them, of the three Christian parties: Nestorius for the Nestorians, Jacob (Mār Yaʿqūb Baradaeus) for the Jacobites, and "Diqyūs" for the imperial church, called below "the Isrāʾīliyyah, the kings of the Christians".}} — one of them said, when God raised Jesus up: he is God; another said: the son of God; and another said: the Word of God and His servant. Then the two slanderers said: my saying is closer to your saying, and your saying to mine, than the saying of this man; so come, let us fight them. So they fought them and set the Children of Israel upon them. Then they brought out from among themselves four men, each people bringing out its learned man, and they disputed about Jesus after he had been raised up. One of them said: he is God, who came down to earth, gave life to whom he gave life and caused to die whom he caused to die, then ascended to heaven — and these are the Nestorians. The other two said: you lie. Then one of the two said to the other: say what you hold about him. He said: he is the third of three: God is a god, he is a god, and his mother is a god — and these are the Isrāʾīliyyah, the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: you lie; he is the servant of God and His messenger, His spirit and His Word — and these are the Muslims. Every man among them had followers according to what he said, and they fought one another, and the Muslims were overcome; and that is the word of God: and kill those among the people who enjoin justice (3:21). Qatādah said: They are the ones of whom God said Then the factions differed: they differed about him and became factions.

### On the interpretation of His words: It is not for God to take any son — glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter He only says to it "Be", and it is. (35) And indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path (36) (19:35–36)

God, Exalted be His mention, says: Those who said "Jesus is the son of God" have disbelieved and have made a monstrous fabrication against Him; for it is not fitting for God to take a son, nor is that proper for Him, nor can it be; rather everything other than Him is His creation. This is like the saying of ʿAmr ibn Aḥmar:

> On the summit of a smooth crag, soaring and lofty, / short of which no plain and no mountain is to be sought.{{fn:The poet describes a mountain: nothing is "sought" (lā yubtaghā), that is, nothing is fitting (lā yanbaghī), beyond it. Al-Ṭabarī cites the line because mā kāna li-llāhi likewise means "it is not fitting for God".}}
And an in His words to take (an yattakhidha) is in the position of the nominative by virtue of kāna.

As for His words glory be to Him: He says, a declaration of God's transcendence and His exoneration from having what the disbelievers attribute to Him, who say "Jesus is the son of God". As for His words When He decrees a matter He only says to it "Be", and it is: He, Majestic is His praise, says: God only originated the creation of Jesus by an act of origination, and brought him into being by an act of bringing-into-being, without any male who impregnated his mother; rather He said to him "Be", and it is, because that is how He originates things and invents them: He only says, when He decrees the creation of a thing or its bringing-into-being, "Be", and it is, existent, newly come into being; the creation of it is not burdensome for Him, because He does not create it with toil and trouble, nor bring it into being with labour and hardship.

As for His words And indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him: the reciters differed in reading this. The generality of the reciters of the people of Medina and Baṣrah read it wa-anna llāha rabbī wa-rabbukum, with fatḥah on anna. The scholars of Arabic differed as to the grounds for the fatḥah of an when it is read with fatḥah. Some of the grammarians of Kūfah said: it is given fatḥah in reference back to "Jesus" and in coordination with him, in the sense: "Such is Jesus son of Mary, and such is the fact that God is my Lord and your Lord"; and if that is so, an is in the nominative, though it may be construed as being in the genitive, as He said That is because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly (6:131). He said: and were it given fatḥah in dependence upon His words and has enjoined upon me — "that God is…" — that would be a possible construction. Some of the Baṣrans used to say — and this is reported also of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who was among those who read it with fatḥah — that an is given fatḥah only on the construal of "and He decreed (qaḍā) that God is my Lord and your Lord". The generality of the Kūfan reciters read it wa-inna llāha, with kasrah on inna, in the sense of being in sequence upon His words He only says to it. And it is reported of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he used to read it "fa-innamā yaqūlu lahu kun fa-yakūn, inna llāha rabbī wa-rabbukum", without the wāw.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The reading we choose in this is the kasrah, as beginning a new sentence. When it is read thus it has no syntactic position; though it may also be a coordination with the inna which accompanies His words He said: I am (innī) the servant of God; He has given me the Scripture … and indeed God is my Lord and your Lord. And were someone among those who read it with the accusative to say: it is in the accusative by coordination with "the Scripture", in the sense "He has given me the Scripture, and He has given me that God is my Lord and your Lord", that would be a fine construction. The meaning of the passage is: I and you, O people, are all servants of God, so worship Him alone and none other.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from one who is not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: He charged them, when he informed them about himself, his birth, his death and his resurrection: Indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path — that is, I and you are servants of God, so worship Him and worship none other.

As for His words this is a straight path: He says, this which I have enjoined upon you, and of which I have informed you that God commanded me, is the straight road, which whoever travels is saved, and whoever takes it is guided, because it is the religion of God which He commanded His prophets.
### On the interpretation of His words: Then the factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a mighty Day (37) (19:37)
God, Exalted be His mention, says: Then those who differed concerning Jesus differed, and became divided factions from among his people; as in:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to me: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, His words Then the factions differed among themselves, he said: the People of the Book.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, His words Then the factions differed among themselves: It was mentioned to us that when the son of Mary was raised up, the Children of Israel chose four of their jurists. They said to the first: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is God; he came down to earth, created what he created and gave life to what he gave life, then ascended to heaven. Some people followed him in that, and they were the Jacobites among the Christians. The other three said: We bear witness that you are a liar. Then they said to the second: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is the son of God. Some people followed him in that, and they were the Nestorians among the Christians. The other two said: We bear witness that you are a liar. Then they said to the third: What do you say about Jesus? He said: He is a god, and his mother is a god, and God is a god. Some people followed him in that, and they were the Isrāʾīliyyah among the Christians. The fourth said: I bear witness that you are a liar; rather he is the servant of God and His messenger; he is the Word of God and His spirit. So the people disputed, and the Muslim man said: I adjure you by God — do you not know that Jesus used to eat food, and that God, Blessed and Exalted, does not eat food? They said: By God, yes. He said: Do you know that Jesus used to sleep? They said: By God, yes. He said: So the Muslim overcame them in argument. He said: Then the people fought one another. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Jacobites prevailed that day and the Muslims were struck down, and God sent down concerning that in the Qurʾān: Indeed those who disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the prophets without right, and kill those among the people who enjoin justice — give them tidings of a painful punishment (3:21).
Al-Ḥasan related to us: Isḥāq informed us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah: Then the factions differed among themselves: they differed about him and became factions.

As for His words so woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a mighty Day: He says, then the valley of Hell which is called Wayl (Woe) is for those who disbelieve in God — those who claim that Jesus is a son to God, and others among the people of disbelief in Him — because of their witnessing a Day mighty in its import, namely the Day of Resurrection.
Qatādah used to say in the interpretation of this what:
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: God said: so woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a mighty Day: they will witness then a mighty terror.
### On the interpretation of His words: And she who guarded her chastity: We breathed into her of Our spirit, and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds (91) (21:91)
God, Exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him): And mention her who guarded her chastity (farj), meaning Mary daughter of ʿImrān.
By His word guarded (aḥṣanat) He means: she preserved her private parts and kept them from what God had forbidden her to permit therein.
There was disagreement about the farj which God, Majestic is His praise, meant that she guarded. Some of them said: He meant by it her own private parts, that she preserved them from indecency.

Others said: He meant by it the opening of her shift, that she kept Gabriel from it before she knew that he was the messenger of her Lord, and before recognition of him was established for her. They said: What indicates this is His words so We breathed into her, which follow upon His words And she who guarded her farj; they said: so it is known thereby that the meaning of the passage is: "And she who guarded the opening of her garment: We breathed into her of Our spirit."

Abū Jaʿfar said: The more fitting of the two opinions in the interpretation of this, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: she guarded her private parts from indecency, because that is the more prevalent of its two meanings and the more apparent in the outward sense of the words. We breathed into her of Our spirit: He says, so We breathed into the opening of her shift of Our spirit. We have mentioned the disagreement of those who differed about the meaning of His words so We breathed into her elsewhere, together with the opinion closer to correctness in that matter, earlier in this work, in a way that dispenses with repeating it in this place.

As for His words and We made her and her son a sign for the worlds: He says, and We made Mary and her son a lesson for the worlds of their time, that they might take a lesson from them and reflect upon their affair, and so know the greatness of Our authority and Our power over whatever We will. He said "a sign" and did not say "two signs", although He mentioned two signs, because the meaning of the passage is: We made the two of them a token and a proof for Us; so each one of them, in respect of indicating God and His great power, stands in the place of the other, since their affair in indicating God is one.

### On the interpretation of His words: And We did give Moses the Scripture, that they might be guided. (49) And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We gave them refuge upon a height, having a settled place and running water (50) (23:49–50)

God, Exalted be His mention, says: And We gave Moses the Torah, that his people of the Children of Israel might be guided by it and act according to what is in it. And We made the son of Mary and his mother: He says, and We made the son of Mary and his mother a proof for Us against those who lived among them, and of Our power to bring bodies into being without an origin, just as We brought the creation of Jesus into being without a father; as in:

Al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, concerning His words And We made the son of Mary and his mother, he said: she bore him without any father of his; and for that reason "sign" is made singular, although He has mentioned Mary and her son.

As for His words and We gave them refuge upon a height: He says, and We gathered them in and brought them to a height. One says "so-and-so took refuge (awā) in such-and-such a place, and he takes refuge (yaʾwī) in it", when he betakes himself to it; and on the pattern of afʿaltuhu, "he gives him refuge (yuʾwīhi)".

As for His words upon a height (rabwah): He means, to a place of the earth raised above what surrounds it; and for that reason it is said of a man who holds an elevated station among his people, with might, honour and numbers: "he is upon a height (rabwah) among his people". In it there are two dialectal forms: ḍammah on the rāʾ and kasrah, when the noun is intended; and when the single act is intended, from the verbal noun, one says rabā rabwatan.
The people of interpretation differed about the place which God described with this description, and in which He gave refuge to Mary and her son. Some of them said: it is al-Ramlah in Palestine.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to me: Ṣafwān ibn ʿĪsā related to us: Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ related to us: a cousin of Abū Hurayrah, called Abū ʿAbd Allāh, related to me, he said: Abū Hurayrah said to us: Keep to this Ramlah of Palestine, for it is the height of which God said and We gave them refuge upon a height, having a settled place and running water.

ʿIṣām ibn Rawwād ibn al-Jarrāḥ related to me: my father related to us: ʿAbbād Abū ʿUtbah al-Khawwāṣ related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿAmr al-Shaybānī related to us, from Ibn Waʿlah, from Kurayb, who said: I do not know what —
Murrah al-Bahzī related to us, that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) — and he mentioned that the height is al-Ramlah.

Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh the cousin of Abū Hurayrah, who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say concerning the words of God upon a height, having a settled place and running water, he said: it is al-Ramlah of Palestine.

Ibn Bashshār related to us: Ṣafwān related to us: Bishr ibn Rāfiʿ related to us: Abū ʿAbd Allāh the cousin of Abū Hurayrah related to me, he said: Abū Hurayrah said to us: Keep to this Ramlah which is in Palestine, for it is the height of which God said and We gave them refuge upon a height, having a settled place and running water.
Others said: it is Damascus.
### Those who said this

Aḥmad ibn al-Walīd al-Qurashī related to us: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us: Shuʿbah related to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that he said concerning this verse, and We gave them refuge upon a height, having a settled place and running water, he said: they claimed that it is Damascus.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: it has reached me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: Damascus.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, the like of it.

Yaḥyā ibn ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Sahmī related to me: Ibn Bukayr related to us: al-Layth ibn Saʿd related to us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah related to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, concerning His words and We gave them refuge upon a height, having a settled place and running water, he said: to a height among the heights (rubā) of Egypt. He said: and the heights are found only in Egypt; when the water is released, the villages stand upon the heights; were it not for the heights, those villages would be drowned.
Others said: it is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).
### Those who said this
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: it is Jerusalem.
He said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: Kaʿb used to say: Jerusalem is nearer to heaven by eighteen miles.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Kaʿb, the like of it.

The most fitting of these opinions in the interpretation of this is that it is an elevated place, possessed of level ground and of visible water; and such is not the description of al-Ramlah, for al-Ramlah has no running water, whereas God, Exalted be His mention, described this height as having a settled place and running water.
A group of the people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, His words and We gave them refuge upon a height, he said: the height is the level place.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, His words upon a height, he said: level.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

As for His words having a settled place and running water: God, Exalted be His mention, says: among the qualities of the height in which We gave refuge to Mary and her son Jesus is that it is a spread-out land and open ground, and possessed of visible — not subterranean — flowing water.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: and running water, he said: maʿīn is flowing water, and it is the river of which God said Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet (19:24).

Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah al-Asadī related to me: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā related to us: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Yaḥyā, from Mujāhid, concerning His words having a settled place and running water, he said: maʿīn is water.

Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah al-Asadī related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: running water (maʿīn), he said: water.
Al-Qāsim related to us: al-Ḥusayn related to us: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār related to me: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt related to us: Sharīk related to us, from Sālim, from Saʿīd, concerning His words having a settled place and running water, he said: the level place; and maʿīn is visible water.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words and running water: it is visible water.
Others said: by "a settled place" He meant fruits.
### Those who said this
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah: having a settled place and running water: it has fruits, and it is Jerusalem.
Al-Ḥasan related to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, the like of it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: This opinion which Qatādah stated concerning the meaning of having a settled place — unless he meant by his statement that it was described as "having a settled place" only on account of the fruits that are in it, and that on their account its inhabitants settle in it — has no basis that we know of. As for maʿīn, it is a passive participle (mafʿūl) from "I saw it with the eye (ʿintuhu), I see it (aʿīnuhu)", so it is maʿīn, "seen"; and it may also be of the pattern faʿīl from maʿana yamʿanu, so it is maʿīn, from al-māʿūn. From this is the saying of ʿAbīd ibn al-Abraṣ:
> A gushing spring, or a running stream flowing far, / or a hill-crag with mountain-clefts before it.

### On the interpretation of His words: So We made them a precedent and an example for those who came after. (56) And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people cry out at it (57) (43:56–57)

The reciters differed in reading this. The generality of the Kūfan reciters other than ʿĀṣim read it fa-jaʿalnāhum sulufan, with ḍammah on the sīn and the lām, construing it as the plural of salīf among people, which is the one who goes ahead in front of the people. Al-Farrāʾ related that he heard al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn mention that he had heard the Arabs say: "a salīf of the people has passed". The generality of the reciters of Medina and Baṣrah, and ʿĀṣim, read it So We made them a precedent (salafan), with fatḥah on the sīn and the lām.

When it is read thus, it may be intended for the group and the individual, the masculine and the feminine, because one says to a people "you are a salaf (predecessor) for us", and it may be pluralised, so that one says "they are aslāf"; from this is the report related from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "The righteous depart as predecessors (aslāfan)."

Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj used to read it fa-jaʿalnāhum sulafan, with ḍammah on the sīn and fatḥah on the lām, construing it as the plural of sulfah among people, like "a community (ummah) of them" and "a portion (qiṭʿah)".

The most correct of the readings in this is the reading of those who read it with fatḥah on the sīn and the lām, because it is the choicest dialect and the speech familiar among the Arabs, and the dialects of the Arabs most entitled to have the Book of God read in them are the most eloquent and the most widely known among them. The interpretation of the passage, then, is: So We made these whom We drowned in the sea, of the people of Pharaoh, a vanguard going ahead into the Fire before the disbelievers of your people, O Muḥammad, of Quraysh; and the disbelievers of your people follow upon their track.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, His words So We made them a precedent and an example for those who came after, he said: the people of Pharaoh — their disbelievers — are a precedent for the disbelievers of the community of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: So We made them a precedent: in the Fire.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar: So We made them a precedent, he said: a precedent to the Fire.

As for His words and an example for those who came after: He says, and a lesson and an admonition by which the nations after them might be admonished, so that they desist from disbelief in God. The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said about this.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: and an example for those who came after, he said: a lesson for those after them.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Abū Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah: and an example for those who came after: that is, an admonition for those who came after.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: and an example for those who came after: that is, an admonition for those after them.
Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: So We made them a precedent and an example, he said: a lesson.

As for His words And when the son of Mary is cited as an example: God, Exalted be His mention, says: And when God likened Jesus, in His bringing him into existence and creating him without a male, to Adam, and compared him to him in that He created him from dust without a male — behold, your people, O Muḥammad, clamour at that and say: Muḥammad wants nothing from us but that we take him as a god whom we worship, as the Christians worshipped the Messiah.
The people of interpretation differed about the interpretation of this. Some of them said the like of what we have said about it.
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour. He said: Quraysh said: Muḥammad only wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: When Jesus son of Mary was mentioned, Quraysh were dismayed at it and said: O Muḥammad, why have you mentioned Jesus son of Mary? And they said: Muḥammad wants nothing but that we should do with him as the Christians did with Jesus son of Mary. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: They cite it to you only for argument (43:58).

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: When Jesus was mentioned in the Qurʾān, the polytheists of Quraysh said: O Muḥammad, what do you intend by mentioning Jesus? He said: And they said: He only wants us to love him as the Christians loved Jesus.

Others said: rather, what was meant by this was the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will come to it (21:98). The polytheists said, when it was sent down: We are content that our gods should be together with Jesus, ʿUzayr and the angels, for all of these are among what is worshipped besides God. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people cry out at it, and they said: Are our gods better, or he? (43:58).
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people cry out at it, he said: He means Quraysh, when it was said to them Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you will come to it (21:98). Quraysh said to him: Then what of the son of Mary? He said: That one is the servant of God and His messenger. They said: By God, this man wants nothing but that we take him as a lord, as the Christians took Jesus son of Mary as a lord. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: They cite it to you only for argument; rather they are a contentious people (43:58).
