The reciters differed in reading His words cry out (yaṣiddūn). The generality of the reciters of Medina, and a group of the reciters of Kūfah, read it yaṣuddūn, with ḍammah on the ṣād; and some of the reciters of Kūfah and Baṣrah read it yaṣiddūn, with kasrah on the ṣād.

The scholars of the speech of the Arabs differed as to the difference between it when it is read with ḍammah on the ṣād and when it is read with kasrah. Some of the grammarians of Baṣrah said — and some of the Kūfans agreed with them on it — that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like yashuddu and yashiddu, and yanummu and yanimmu from namīmah (tale-bearing). Another of them said: whoever reads it with kasrah on the ṣād, its sense is "they clamour", and whoever reads it with ḍammah, its sense is "they turn aside". And some of those who read it with kasrah said: he intended "they clamour", whereas whoever read it with ḍammah intended turning away (ṣudūd) from the truth.

And I was told on the authority of al-Farrāʾ, who said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to me that ʿĀṣim abandoned yaṣuddūn from the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān{{fn:Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, ʿĀṣim's teacher in recitation.}} and read yaṣiddūn. He said: Abū Bakr said: ʿĀṣim related to me, from Abū Razīn, from Abū Yaḥyā, that Ibn ʿAbbās met the nephew of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr and said: Your uncle is indeed an Arab, so how is it that he commits a solecism in His words "idhā qawmuka minhu yaṣuddūn", when it is only yaṣiddūn?

The correct opinion on this is that they are two well-known readings and two famous dialectal forms with one meaning. We have not found the people of interpretation distinguishing between the meaning of this when it is read with ḍammah and with kasrah; and had its meaning been different, disagreement about its interpretation among its people would have existed, as the disagreement over its reading according to the two dialectal forms exists. But since its meaning is not different, they did not disagree that its interpretation is: "they clamour and are dismayed". So with whichever of the two readings the reciter reads, he is correct.
### Mention of what we have said in the interpretation of this
ʿAlī related to me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, His words behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: behold, your people cry out at it: He says, they clamour.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us: Abū Ḥamzah related to us, from al-Mughīrah al-Ḍabbī, from al-Ṣaʿb ibn ʿUthmān, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to read behold, your people cry out at it (yaṣiddūn), and he used to explain it, saying: they clamour.
Ibn Bashshār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour.
Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us; both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning the words of God, Mighty and Majestic, behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: behold, your people cry out at it: that is, they are dismayed and clamour.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read it yaṣiddūn: that is, they clamour; and ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) read yaṣuddūn.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour.
Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: behold, your people cry out at it, he said: they clamour.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not put it to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people. (58) He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. (59) And had We willed, We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding. (60) (43:58–60)
He says, Exalted be His remembrance: And the polytheists of your people said, O Muḥammad: Are our gods which we worship better, or Muḥammad — so that we should worship Muḥammad and abandon our gods?
It was mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb this is: "Are our gods better, or this one?"
### The report concerning this

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, that in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is: "And they said, Are our gods better, or this one?" — meaning by it Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).
Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is: Are our gods better, or Jesus?
### Those who said this

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His words And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not put it to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people (43:58): he said: They disputed with him and said: He claims that everyone who is worshipped besides God is in the Fire; well then, we are content that our gods should be together with Jesus, Ezra and the angels — these have all been worshipped besides God. He said: So God sent down the exoneration of Jesus.
Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words Are our gods better (43:58): he said: These people worshipped Jesus, and we worship the angels.
### On His words: They did not put it to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people (43:58), up to upon the earth, succeeding (43:60)

As for His words, Exalted be His remembrance, They did not put it to you except for argument, He says, Exalted be His remembrance: They did not set forth this parable to you, O Muḥammad, nor did they say this saying to you, except out of argument and contention with which they contend against you. rather, they are a contentious people: He says, Majestic is His praise: There is not in these polytheists of your people, O Muḥammad, in their disputing with you by that with which they dispute with you, any seeking of the truth; rather, they are a contentious people, who seek out contention by means of falsehood.
It is mentioned from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "No people ever strayed from the truth except that they were given to argument."
### The report concerning this

Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Yaʿlā related to us: al-Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār related to us, from Abū Ghālib, from Abū Umāmah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No people ever strayed after guidance which they had been upon, except that they were given to argument," and he recited: They did not put it to you except for argument ... to the end of the verse (43:58).

Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Kindī and Abū Kurayb related to me, both saying: Muḥammad ibn Bishr related to us: Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār related to us, from Abū Umāmah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qurʾān, and he grew exceedingly angry, until it was as though vinegar had been poured over his face; then he said (peace and blessings be upon him): "Do not strike one part of the Book of God against another, for no people have ever strayed except that they were given to argument." Then he recited: They did not put it to you except for argument; rather, they are a contentious people (43:58).
### On His words: He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour (43:59)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: Jesus is nothing but a servant from among Our servants, upon whom We bestowed favour by granting him success and faith, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel; He says: and We made him a sign for the Children of Israel, and a proof for Us against them by Our sending him to them to call them to Us. And he is not as the Christians say, that he is the son of God, Exalted — exalted is God above that.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said concerning that.
### Those who said this

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: He was only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour (43:59): by that He means Jesus son of Mary; Jesus son of Mary was nothing beyond that — he was nothing but a servant upon whom God bestowed favour.
They also said the like of what we have said concerning His words and We made him an example for the Children of Israel (43:59).
### Those who said this
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Qatādah: an example for the Children of Israel (43:59) — I think he said: a sign for the Children of Israel.
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: and We made him an example for the Children of Israel (43:59), that is, a sign.
### On His words: And had We willed, We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: And had We willed, O company of the children of Adam, We would have destroyed you and annihilated you all, and set in your place upon the earth angels who would succeed you in it and worship Me. That is like His words, Exalted be His remembrance: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and God is ever Able to do that (4:133), and as He said: If He wills, He can remove you and cause to succeed after you whomever He wills (6:133).
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said concerning that, except that some of them said: its meaning is: succeeding one another.
### Those who said this

ʿAlī related to me: Abū Ṣāliḥ related to us: Muʿāwiyah related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words And had We willed, We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60): He says: succeeding one another.

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us — both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60): he said: populating the earth in your place.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, concerning His words angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60): he said: succeeding one another, in the place of the children of Adam.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: And had We willed, We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60): had God willed, He would have set upon the earth angels succeeding one another.

Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: And had We willed, We could have made of you angels upon the earth, succeeding (43:60): he said: as successors in your place.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour, so do not doubt it, but follow Me; this is a straight path. (61) And let not Satan avert you; indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy. (62) (43:61–62)
The people of interpretation differed concerning the pronoun (hāʾ) in His words And indeed, he, as to what is meant by it and to whom or what it refers.

- Some of them said: It refers to Jesus, and it goes back to him. They said: The meaning of the words is: And indeed Jesus — his appearance is a knowledge by which the coming of the Hour is known, because his appearance is one of its signs, and his descent to the earth is an indication of the passing away of this world and the approach of the Hereafter.
### Those who said this

Ibn Bashshār related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us: Sufyān related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Yaḥyā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): he said: the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary.
Ibn al-Muthannā related to us: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, the like of it, except that he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary.

Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Aḥmasī related to me: Ghālib ibn Qāʾid related to us: Qays related to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to read "And indeed, he is a sign (ʿalam) of the Hour"{{fn:A variant reading, la-ʿalamun ("a sign, a token"), with a fatḥah on the ʿayn, in place of the standard la-ʿilmun ("knowledge").}}; he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary.

Abū Kurayb related to us: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah related to us, from Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq, from Jābir, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: I do not know whether the people have learnt the interpretation of this verse, or whether they have not grasped it: "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour"; he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary.

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour": he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary.

Yaʿqūb related to me: Hushaym related to us: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Abū Mālik, and from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, that the two of them said concerning His words And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): they both said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary; and one of the two read it "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour".

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to us: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us — both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): he said: a sign of the Hour is the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary before the Day of Resurrection.

Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour": he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary is a sign of the Hour — the Resurrection.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, concerning His words "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour": he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary is a sign of the Hour.

Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): he said: the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary before the Day of Resurrection.

I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): meaning the coming forth of Jesus son of Mary and his descent from heaven before the Day of Resurrection.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61): he said: the descent of Jesus son of Mary is a knowledge of the Hour, when he descends.

- Others said: The pronoun in His words And indeed, he refers to the Qurʾān. They said: The meaning of the words is: And indeed this Qurʾān is a knowledge of the Hour: it teaches you of its coming to pass, and informs you about it and about its terrors.
### Those who said this
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, who said: al-Ḥasan used to say: "And indeed, he is a sign of the Hour" — this Qurʾān.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: People used to say: The Qurʾān is a knowledge of the Hour.

The reciters of the garrison cities were agreed, in the reading of His words And indeed, he is knowledge of the Hour (43:61), upon a kasrah on the ʿayn of ʿilm; and there has been related from Ibn ʿAbbās what I have mentioned from him concerning a fatḥah upon it, and likewise from Qatādah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
The correct reading in this is the kasrah on the ʿayn, because of the consensus of the authoritative body of reciters upon it.

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy this is "And indeed, he is a reminder (dhikr) of the Hour", and that confirms the reading of those who read with a kasrah on the ʿayn in His words knowledge.
### On His words: so do not doubt it (43:61)
He says: So be in no doubt about it or about its coming, O people.
As:
Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: so do not doubt it (43:61): he said: do not be in doubt about it.
### On His words: but follow Me (43:61)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: and obey Me — so act upon what I have commanded you, and desist from what I have forbidden you. this is a straight path: He says: your following Me, O people, in My command and My prohibition is a straight path; He says: a road in which there is no crookedness; rather, it is upright.
### On His words: And let not Satan avert you (43:62)

He says, Majestic is His praise: And let not Satan turn you aside from obedience to Me in what I command you and forbid you, so that you forsake it for something else and swerve from the straight path and go astray. indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy: He says: Satan is to you an enemy who calls you to that in which lies your destruction and turns you away from the right course of the way, in order to bring you down into the places of ruin; manifest — he has made his enmity to you manifest by his refusal to prostrate to your father Adam, and by his beguiling him with delusion until he brought him out of the Garden, out of envy and insolence.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: And when Jesus came with the clear proofs, he said: I have come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that wherein you differ; so fear God and obey me. (63) Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path. (64) (43:63–64)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: And when Jesus came to the Children of Israel with the clear proofs, meaning the evident indications. And it was said that what is meant by the clear proofs is the Gospel.
### Those who said this
Bishr related to us: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: And when Jesus came with the clear proofs (43:63), that is, with the Gospel.
### On His words: he said: I have come to you with wisdom (43:63)
It was said that what is meant by wisdom in this place is prophethood.
### Those who said this
Muḥammad related to me: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: he said: I have come to you with wisdom (43:63): he said: prophethood.

I have already explained the meaning of wisdom in what has gone before of this book of ours, together with its evidences, and I have mentioned the disagreement of those who differed concerning its interpretation, and that dispenses with repeating it.
### On His words: and to make clear to you some of that wherein you differ (43:63)
He says: and to make clear to you, O company of the Children of Israel, some of that wherein you differ of the rulings of the Torah.
As:

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me: al-Ḥasan related to us: Warqāʾ related to us — both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words and to make clear to you some of that wherein you differ (43:63): he said: of the alteration of the Torah.

It has been said that the meaning of "some" in this place is in the sense of "all", and they made that analogous to the saying of Labīd{{fn:Labīd ibn Rabīʿah, the pre-Islamic poet whose ode is one of the Muʿallaqāt; the line is from that ode.}}:
> One who forsakes places whenever I am not pleased with them,
> unless their fated death should lay hold of some of the souls.

They said: Death does not lay hold of "some" of the souls; the meaning is only: unless their fated death should lay hold of the souls. But there is no great sense in what this speaker said, because Jesus said to them and to make clear to you some of that wherein you differ only because there had been among them much disagreement about the affairs of their religion and their worldly life; so he said to them: I shall make clear to you some of that — namely the affair of their religion, apart from the affairs of their worldly life about which they differed; and for that reason he specified what he informed them that he would make clear to them. As for the saying of Labīd, "unless it should lay hold of some of the souls", he too said that in the same way, because he meant: unless its fated death should lay hold of his own soul; and his soul, from among all souls, is without doubt a part and not the whole.
### On His words: so fear God and obey me (43:63)

He says: So fear your Lord, O people, by obeying Him, and dread Him by shunning acts of disobedience to Him; and obey me in what I have commanded you of fearing God and following His command, and of accepting my sincere counsel to you.
### On His words: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him (43:64)

He says: Indeed God — He who has the right over us that we single Him out alone in divinity and devote obedience sincerely to Him — is my Lord and the Lord of all of you; so worship Him alone, and do not associate anything with Him in worship of Him, for that is not fitting, nor is it proper that anything other than He should be worshipped.
### On His words: this is a straight path (43:64)

He says: This which I have commanded you — the fearing of God, obedience to me, and the singling out of God alone in divinity — is the straight road, and it is the religion of God, other than which He accepts nothing from any one of His servants.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: But the factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day. (65) Do they await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive? (66) (43:65–66)
The people of interpretation differed concerning those meant by the factions (aḥzāb) whom God mentioned in this place.
- Some of them said: By that He meant the group who debated with one another over the matter of Jesus and differed about him.
### Those who said this

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, concerning His words But the factions differed among themselves (43:65): he said: They are the four whom the Children of Israel sent forth, who spoke concerning Jesus.{{fn:An allusion to the account, related elsewhere on Qatādah's authority, that the Children of Israel put forward four of their learned men to pronounce on Jesus, and that each gave a different answer about his nature, whence the sects of the Christians arose.}}
- Others said: Rather, they are the Jews and the Christians.
### Those who said this
Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His words But the factions differed among themselves (43:65): he said: the Jews and the Christians.

The correct opinion on this is to say: Its meaning is: So the sects who differed concerning Jesus son of Mary — from among those whom Jesus called to what he called them to, the fearing of God and acting in obedience to Him — differed among themselves; and they are the Jews and the Christians, and those of the Christians who differed about him; for all of them were factions, scowling in hostility, of divergent desires, despite his making plain to them the matter of his own self and his saying to them: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path (43:64).
### On His words: so woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day (43:65)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: So the valley (wayl) that flows with pus and purulence in Hell is for those who disbelieved in God, who said of Jesus son of Mary other than what Jesus described himself as being in this verse. from the punishment of a painful day: He says: from the punishment of a day that inflicts pain; and the day is described as inflicting pain since the punishment that pains them takes place in it — and that is the Day of Resurrection.
As:
Muḥammad related to us: Aḥmad related to us: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: from the punishment of a painful day (43:65): he said: from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: Then We sent following in their footsteps Our messengers, and We followed them with Jesus son of Mary and gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy; and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it for them — only seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance. So We gave those who believed among them their reward, but many of them are transgressors. (27) (57:27)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: Then We sent, following in their footsteps, Our messengers whom We sent with the clear proofs in the footsteps of Noah and Abraham — Our messengers — and We followed them with Jesus son of Mary; and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him, meaning those who followed Jesus upon his way and his law, compassion, which is the most intense form of mercy, and mercy; and monasticism they invented: He says: they originated it; We did not prescribe it for them: He says: We did not make that monasticism obligatory upon them; only seeking the good pleasure of God: He says: but they invented it seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance.
The people of interpretation differed concerning those who did not observe monasticism with its due observance.
- Some of them said: They are those who invented it; they did not carry it out, but rather altered and departed from the religion of God with which He sent Jesus, and became Christians and Jews.

- Others said: Rather, they are a people who came after those who invented it and did not observe it with its due observance, because they were unbelievers; but they said: We shall do as those did who did that originally. So they are the ones whom God described as not having observed it with its due observance.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said in the interpretation of these expressions, up to the point at which we mentioned that the people of interpretation differ about it.
### Those who said this

Bishr related to me: Yazīd related to us: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy (57:27): these two are from God; but monasticism a people invented of their own accord, and it was not prescribed for them; rather they sought by it, and intended, the good pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its due observance. It was mentioned to us that they renounced women and took to cells (ṣawāmiʿ).

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah: and monasticism they invented (57:27): he said: it was not prescribed for them; they invented it seeking the good pleasure of God.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words We did not prescribe it for them (57:27): he said: Then why? He said: They invented it seeking the good pleasure of God, as a voluntary act; but they did not observe it with its due observance.
### Those who said: those who did not observe monasticism with its due observance were other than those who invented it, but were people who wished to emulate them

Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥurayth, Abū ʿAmmār al-Marwazī, related to us: al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: There were kings after Jesus who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and there were among them believers who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their king: We find nothing harder upon us than the reviling with which these people revile us, for they read and whoever does not judge by what God has sent down — those are the unbelievers (5:44), these verses, together with the faults they find in us in their reading; so summon them, and let them read as we read and believe as we have believed. He said: So he summoned them and gathered them, and offered them death, or else that they abandon the reading of the Torah and the Gospel save what they had altered of them. They said: What do you want by that? Leave us be! He said: Then a party of them said: Build us a pillar, then raise us up onto it, then give us something by which we may draw up our food and drink, and we shall not come back to you. And a party of them said: Leave us to wander in the land and roam, and drink as the wild beasts drink; and if you get hold of us in your land, kill us. And a party said: Build us dwellings in the wastelands, and we shall dig wells and cultivate vegetables, and we shall not come back to you nor pass by you — and there was not one of these but he had a close kinsman among them. He said: So they did that, and God, Majestic is His praise, sent down and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it for them — only seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27). The later ones said: We shall devote ourselves to worship as so-and-so devoted himself, and wander as so-and-so wandered, and take dwellings as so-and-so took — while they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they emulated. He said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent, and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his cell, a wanderer came from his wandering, and the dweller came from his dwelling, and they believed in him and affirmed him. So God, Majestic is His praise, said: O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two portions of His mercy (57:28). He said: two rewards, for their faith in Jesus and their affirmation of the Torah and the Gospel, and their faith in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and their affirmation of him. He said: and make for you a light by which you may walk (57:28): the Qurʾān, and their following the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). And He said: so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God, and that bounty is in the hand of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty (57:29).

Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ṭālib related to us: Dāwud ibn al-Muḥabbar related to us: al-Ṣaʿq ibn Ḥazn related to us: ʿAqīl al-Jaʿdī related to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Those who were before us split into seventy-one sects, of which three were saved and the rest perished. One sect of the three confronted the kings and fought them over the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary (the blessings of God be upon them), and the kings killed them. And one sect had no strength to confront the kings, so they remained in the midst of their people, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus son of Mary (the blessings of God be upon him), and the kings killed them and sawed them asunder with saws. And one sect had no strength either to confront the kings or to remain in the midst of their people calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus (the blessings of God be upon him), so they betook themselves to the deserts and the mountains and became monks there; and that is the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it for them." He said: they did it only seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance: he said: those who came after them did not observe it with its due observance; So We gave those who believed among them their reward: he said: and they are those who believed in me and affirmed me. He said: but many of them are transgressors: he said: and they are those who denied me and called me a liar.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us: Mihrān related to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it (57:27): he said: The later ones, from among those of the people of polytheism who devoted themselves to worship, after those of them who had passed away had passed away, would say: We shall devote ourselves to worship as so-and-so devoted himself, and wander as so-and-so wandered — while they were in their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they emulated.
### Those who said: those who did not observe it with its due observance were those who invented it

Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me: my father related to me: my paternal uncle related to me: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy up to His words with its due observance (57:27): He says: they did not obey Me in it, and they spoke in it with disobedience to God. That is because God, Mighty and Majestic, had prescribed fighting for them before He sent Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him); and when the people of faith had been rooted out and only a few of them remained, and the people of polytheism had grown many, and the messengers had gone and been overpowered, they withdrew into the caves, and that state persisted with them until a party of them disbelieved and abandoned the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, and His religion, and took up innovation and Christianity and Judaism, and so did not observe it with its due observance; while a party remained firm upon the religion of Jesus son of Mary (the blessings of God be upon him), as it was when he came to them with the clear proofs, and God, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muḥammad as a messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) while they were in that state; and that is His word: O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you two portions of His mercy up to and God is Forgiving, Merciful (57:28).

I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it for them (57:27): God, Mighty and Majestic, had prescribed fighting for them before Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent; and when the people of faith had been rooted out and only the few of them remained, and the people of polytheism had grown many, and the messengers had ceased, they withdrew from the people and came to be in the caves, and they remained so until a party of them changed, and abandoned the religion of God and His command and His covenant which He had made with them, and took up innovations, and invented Christianity and Judaism; so God, Mighty and Majestic, said to them: but they did not observe it with its due observance; while a party of them remained firm upon the religion of Jesus (the blessings of God be upon him) until God sent Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and they believed in him.

Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm related to me: Hushaym related to us: Zakariyyā ibn Abī Maryam informed us, saying: I heard Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī say: God has prescribed for you the fasting of Ramaḍān, but He has not prescribed for you its night vigil; the night vigil is only something you have innovated. And a people innovated an innovation that God had not prescribed for them, seeking by it the good pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its due observance, and so God censured them for abandoning it, saying: and monasticism they invented — We did not prescribe it for them — only seeking the good pleasure of God; but they did not observe it with its due observance (57:27).

The most likely of the opinions on this to be correct is to say: Those whom God described as not having observed monasticism with its due observance were some of the groups which invented it. That is because God, Majestic is His praise, informed that He gave those who believed among them their reward; and so He indicated thereby that among them were those who did observe it with its due observance, for had there not been among them those who were such, there would have been no one deserving of the reward of which He, Majestic is His praise, said: So We gave those who believed among them their reward. Only, those who did not observe it with its due observance may have been in the time of those who invented it, and may have been after them; for when those who are their descendants did not observe it, it is permissible in the speech of the Arabs to say: the people did not observe it, in general terms, while those meant by it are the part of them who were present. The like of this has already been dealt with in many places in this book.
### On His words: So We gave those who believed among them their reward (57:27)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: So We gave those who believed in God and His messengers from among these people who invented monasticism their recompense, in the Hereafter, for their seeking the good pleasure of God and their faith in Him and in His Messenger; but many of them are people of acts of disobedience, who have departed from obedience to Him and from faith in Him.
The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said concerning that.
### Those who said this
Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said: So We gave those who believed among them their reward (57:27): he said: those who observed that properly.

### On the interpretation of His words, Exalted: And when Jesus son of Mary said: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me whose name is Aḥmad. But when he came to them with the clear proofs, they said: This is manifest sorcery. (6) (61:6)

He says, Exalted be His remembrance: And remember also, O Muḥammad, when Jesus son of Mary said to his people of the Children of Israel: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah which was sent down upon Moses, and bringing good tidings — I give you good tidings — of a messenger to come after me whose name is Aḥmad.

Yūnus related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ informed me, from Saʿīd ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Hilāl al-Sulamī, from ʿIrbāḍ ibn Sāriyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "I was, with God, written down as the Seal of the Prophets while Adam was still lying prostrate in his clay; and I shall tell you of the first of that: the prayer of my father Abraham, the good tidings of Jesus concerning me, and the vision which my mother saw — and so it is with the mothers of the prophets, they see visions — that she saw, when she gave birth to me, that there came forth from her a light by which the palaces of Syria were lit up."

But when he came to them with the clear proofs: He says: but when Aḥmad came to them with the clear proofs — which are the indications that God gave him as proofs of his prophethood — they said: This is manifest sorcery: He says: what he has brought is nothing other than sorcery, and he is but a sorcerer.
